title: Aqeedah
sub: Learn about Allah, His Messengers ﷺ and the Last Day

lessons.title: Why we learn belief
lessons.about: Why every Muslim must know what is necessary, impossible and possible for Allah.

cards.x: Aqeedah means belief: what a Muslim holds to be true in the heart. Every Muslim who has reached adulthood and is sane must know what is necessary for Allah, what is impossible for Him, and what is possible for Him, and the same for the Messengers عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

cards.x: Scholars sort everything the mind can think of into three. Necessary (wajib): the mind cannot picture it not being there, like Allah's existence. Impossible (mustahil): the mind cannot picture it existing, like Allah having a partner. Possible (ja'iz): it may exist or not, like rain tomorrow.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

cards.x: Knowing these things protects your belief from doubt. You don't need to be a scholar: you need to know them clearly and be sure of them.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

checks.q: Knowing what is necessary, impossible and possible for Allah is a duty on whom?
checks.a: Every sane Muslim who has reached adulthood
w: Only people who were not born Muslim
checks.why: Umm al-Barahin makes it a duty on every sane adult Muslim, not only on scholars, because belief must rest on knowledge.

checks.q: In aqeedah, something the mind cannot picture not existing is called…
checks.why: Necessary means the mind cannot picture it absent. Allah's existence is the clearest example.

checks.q: In aqeedah, something that may exist or may not, like rain tomorrow, is called…
checks.why: Everything in creation is possible: it can be or not be, and only exists because Allah brings it into being.

checks.q: Allah having a partner is, for the mind…
checks.why: The mind cannot picture two gods each in full control, so a partner for Allah is impossible.

lessons.title: Islam, Iman and Ihsan
lessons.about: The famous hadith of Jibril: the three levels of the religion.

cards.x: Jibril عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ came in the form of a man and asked the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, Iman, Ihsan and the Hour, so the Companions could learn their religion. Muslim narrated it from 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

cards.ar: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَٰمُ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ الْكِتَٰبَ إِلَّا مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ ﴿١٩﴾
cards.x: Truly, the religion with Allah is Islam.
To bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, pay zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj if you are able.
To believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its bad.
To worship Allah as though you see Him; and though you do not see Him, He sees you.

checks.q: In the hadith of Jibril, how many pillars of Islam are there?
checks.why: The two testimonies, prayer, zakat, fasting Ramadan and Hajj for those able.

checks.q: Which of these is one of the six articles of Iman, not a pillar of Islam?
checks.why: Islam is the outward pillars; Iman is what is believed in the heart.

checks.q: What is Ihsan?
checks.a: Worshipping Allah as though you see Him
checks.why: And though you do not see Him, He sees you. It is the highest level of the religion.

checks.q: Who came asking the Prophet ﷺ these questions?
checks.a: Jibril عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, in the form of a man
w: An angel no one could see
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said afterwards: that was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion.

lessons.title: How we know Allah exists
lessons.about: Imam al-Sanusi's proof from the world around us.

cards.x: Look at the world: things move then stop, grow then fade, arrive then leave. Each new state had a beginning. Imam al-Sanusi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says something that is never free of changes that begin must itself have begun. So the world came into being; it has not always been there.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, proof of His existence

cards.ar: أَمْ خُلِقُواْ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ الْخَٰلِقُونَ ﴿٣٥﴾
cards.x: Or were they created by nothing, or are they themselves the creators?
Something that came into being cannot bring itself into being, just as a house does not build itself. So the world needs a Maker who did not come into being: Allah.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, proof of His existence

cards.x: Imam al-Sanusi gives a proof for each attribute he mentions, so that the believer holds each one with understanding and not only by copying others (taqlid).
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the proofs of the attributes

checks.q: Imam al-Sanusi proves the world had a beginning. What does he point to?
w: Everything in it is very old
checks.why: Things move then stop, grow then fade. Each new state began, and something never free of beginnings must itself have begun.

checks.q: Once we know the world had a beginning, why does it need a Maker?
checks.a: Something that began cannot bring itself into being
w: Something so vast cannot be explained by chance
Something so ordered must have been designed by people
Something that began will one day end by itself
checks.why: A house does not build itself. What came into being needs someone to bring it into being: Allah.

checks.q: Could the Maker of the world also have had a beginning?
checks.a: No, otherwise He too would need a maker, without end
w: Yes, as long as it began before the world
Yes, if it began at the same moment as the world
We cannot know, so we leave it to the scholars
checks.why: If the Maker began, He would need a maker, and that one another, forever. So the Maker has no beginning.

checks.q: Why does al-Sanusi give a proof for each attribute of Allah?
checks.a: So the believer holds belief with understanding, not only by copying
w: So the believer can win every debate with others
So the believer can leave faith and rely on proofs
So the book matches the books of the philosophers
checks.why: He wants each Muslim to know why, so their belief is firm against doubt.

lessons.title: Allah exists, without beginning or end
lessons.about: Allah exists, with no beginning and no end, depending on nothing.

cards.x: Allah exists. His existence has no cause and does not depend on anything.

cards.ar: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْأٓخِرُ وَالظَّـٰهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of all things.
Allah has no beginning (qidam). Everything else came into being after not existing; He did not.
Allah has no end (baqa'). He will never cease to be. As Imam al-Tahawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says: He is Eternal without a beginning and Everlasting without an end.

checks.q: Allah has no beginning (qidam). What does that mean?
checks.a: He never came into being; He always was
w: He was created before everything else
He began when the universe began
checks.why: Qidam means Allah never came into being. Everything else existed after not existing; He did not.

checks.q: Allah has no end (baqa'). What does that mean?
checks.a: He will never cease to exist
w: He will end after the Last Day
He ends when the world ends
checks.why: Baqa' means He never ceases. Al-Tahawi: Eternal without a beginning, Everlasting without an end.

checks.q: Does Allah's existence depend on anything, the way ours depends on Him?
checks.why: Allah's existence has no cause. Everything else depends on Him.

checks.q: Why must Allah have no beginning?
checks.a: If He had a beginning, He would need a maker, like everything that begins
w: Because the world is very old, so He must be older
Because time began with Him, so He is its start
Because the angels testify that He came first
checks.why: Anything that begins needs a cause. Allah needs nothing, so He has no beginning.

lessons.title: Allah is unlike anything
lessons.about: Allah does not resemble His creation, needs nothing, and is One.

cards.x: Allah does not resemble anything He created. He is not a body, He is not in a place, and He is not bound by time. 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' (al-Shura 11)

cards.ar: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ﴿١﴾ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ﴿٢﴾ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ﴿٣﴾ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدُ ﴿٤﴾
cards.x: Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Self-Sufficient on whom all depend. He does not beget, nor was He begotten. And there is none equal to Him.

cards.ar: فَاطِرُ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالْأَرْضِ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجٗا وَمِنَ الْأَنْعَٰمِ أَزْوَٰجٗا يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٞ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ ﴿١١﴾
cards.x: There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
Allah stands by Himself (qiyam bi-nafsihi): He needs no place and no one to bring Him into being. Everything needs Him.
Allah is One (wahdaniyyah): One in His Self, One in His attributes and One in His actions. He has no partner and no equal.

checks.q: Which of these is true about Allah?
checks.a: He does not resemble anything He created
w: He has a body unlike ours
He is in one particular place
He is bound by time like us
checks.why: Allah is not a body, not in a place and not bound by time. 'There is nothing like Him.' (al-Shura 11)

checks.q: Allah 'stands by Himself' (qiyam bi-nafsihi). What does that mean?
checks.a: He needs nothing, while everything needs Him
w: He sits on His Throne, which holds Him up
He stands in one place above His creation
He needs our worship, while we need His mercy
checks.why: He needs no place and no one to bring Him into being, while all things need Him.

checks.q: Allah is One (wahdaniyyah). His Oneness covers…
checks.a: His Self, His attributes and His actions
w: His Self only, while His actions are shared
His Self and His attributes, but not His actions
His actions only, since His Self is unknown
checks.why: No one shares His Self, no one has attributes like His, and no one else truly creates.

checks.q: Which verse sums up that Allah is unlike creation?
checks.a: 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing'
w: 'Read in the name of your Lord'
'Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth'
'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak'
checks.why: Al-Shura 11 denies any likeness, and still affirms hearing and sight, without likeness.

lessons.title: Seven attributes of Allah
lessons.about: Power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech.

cards.x: Allah has Power (qudrah) over every possible thing, and Will (iradah): nothing happens except what He wills.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.ar: اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٖ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ لِتَعْلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٖ قَدِيرٞ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمَا ﴿١٢﴾
cards.x: …so that you may know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge.
Allah has Knowledge ('ilm) of everything: what was, what is, what will be, and what would be. He is Living (hayah) with a life unlike ours.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: Allah hears (sam') and sees (basar) all that exists, without ears or eyes. He speaks (kalam) with an eternal speech that is not letters or sounds. The Qur'an is His speech.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: Umm al-Barahin lists twenty necessary attributes. Existence (wujud). Five that negate what does not befit Him (salbiyyah): no beginning, no end, unlike creation, needing nothing, and Oneness. Seven attributes of meaning (ma'ani): power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech. And seven that follow from those: that He is Powerful, Willing, Knowing, Living, Hearing, Seeing and Speaking.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: The Maturidis, the school of Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ followed by most Hanafis, add an eighth attribute of meaning: takwin, Allah's bringing things into being. The Ash'aris count this under power and will. Both schools are Ahl al-Sunnah.

checks.q: Allah has the attribute of will (iradah). So in creation…
checks.a: Nothing happens except what He wills
checks.why: Nothing happens in His kingdom except what He wills, good or bad.

checks.q: Allah hears and sees. How?
checks.a: Without ears or eyes, unlike creation
w: With ears and eyes like ours
He does not hear or see
checks.why: His attributes are real but unlike ours. He hears every sound and sees everything without organs.

checks.q: Allah's attribute of speech (kalam) is…
checks.a: Eternal, and not made of letters or sounds
w: Created, and made of letters and sounds
Eternal, but made of Arabic letters and sounds
Began with the first revelation to the Prophets
checks.why: His speech has no beginning. The Qur'an is His speech.

checks.q: How many necessary attributes does Umm al-Barahin list?
checks.why: One of existence, five negating, seven of meaning and seven that follow from them: twenty.

checks.q: What extra attribute do the Maturidis count, that the Ash'aris place under power and will?
w: Hearing: Allah's perceiving of all sounds
Mercy: Allah's kindness to His creation
checks.why: Both views are Ahl al-Sunnah. It is a difference of how to count, not of belief in Allah's perfection.

lessons.title: The twenty attributes
lessons.about: The full list from Umm al-Barahin, and what each group means.

cards.x: The first attribute is existence (wujud): Allah truly exists. Al-Sanusi calls it the attribute of the Self (nafsiyyah).
Five attributes deny what does not befit Allah (salbiyyah): no beginning (qidam), no end (baqa'), unlike creation (mukhalafah), needing nothing (qiyam bi-nafsihi) and Oneness (wahdaniyyah).
Seven real attributes (ma'ani): power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech.
Seven more follow from those (ma'nawiyyah): that He is Powerful, Willing, Knowing, Living, Hearing, Seeing and Speaking.

checks.q: Which attribute does al-Sanusi call the attribute of the Self (nafsiyyah)?
checks.why: Existence is first: all the other attributes are of the One who exists.

checks.q: Which group are 'no beginning, no end, unlike creation, needing nothing, Oneness'?
w: The names of the Prophet ﷺ
checks.why: Each one denies something that does not befit Allah.

checks.q: Which is one of the seven attributes of meaning (ma'ani)?
checks.why: The seven of meaning: power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech.

checks.q: 'Allah is Knowing' follows from which attribute?
checks.why: Each of the seven that follow comes from one of the seven of meaning.

checks.q: How many attributes in total are necessary for Allah, in Umm al-Barahin?
checks.why: 1 + 5 + 7 + 7 = 20. His perfection is without limit; these are what every Muslim must know in detail.

lessons.title: The Speech of Allah
lessons.about: The Qur'an is Allah's speech, not created like ours.

cards.x: Allah speaks with an eternal speech. The Qur'an is the speech of Allah: it came from Him, without asking how, and He sent it down to His Messenger ﷺ as revelation.

cards.ar: وَرُسُلٗا قَدْ قَصَصْنَٰهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَرُسُلٗا لَّمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ عَلَيْكَ وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكْلِيمٗا ﴿١٦٤﴾
cards.x: And Allah spoke to Musa directly.

cards.ar: وَإِنْ أَحَدٞ مِّنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ اسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلَٰمَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٞ لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿٦﴾
cards.x: If one of the idolaters seeks your protection, grant it to him so that he may hear the speech of Allah.
The believers are certain it is truly Allah's speech, not created like the speech of creation. Whoever hears it and claims it is human speech has disbelieved.

Imam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ said: the Qur'an is written in the copies, preserved in the hearts and recited by the tongues. Our pronouncing, writing and reciting it are created; the Qur'an itself is not created.

checks.q: What is the Qur'an, according to Imam al-Tahawi?
checks.a: The speech of Allah, not created
w: The speech of Allah, created when revealed
The words of the Prophet ﷺ, inspired by Allah
The words of Jibril, sent down to the Prophet ﷺ
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: it came from Allah and is not created like the speech of creation.

checks.q: Imam Abu Hanifah says some things about the Qur'an are created. Which?
checks.a: Our reciting and writing of it
w: The Qur'an itself, which came down in time
Allah's speech, since it is in Arabic
Its meanings, though not its words
checks.why: Our voices, ink and paper are created. The Qur'an itself, Allah's speech, is not.

checks.q: Where is the Qur'an, according to Imam Abu Hanifah in al-Fiqh al-Akbar?
checks.a: Written in copies, kept in hearts, recited by tongues
w: Only in the copies, which are its true home
Only in the hearts of those who memorise it
Only in the Preserved Tablet, not on earth
checks.why: He described it in all three ways, while it remains Allah's uncreated speech.

checks.q: Someone hears the Qur'an recited and says 'this is just human speech'. What does al-Tahawi say?
w: He is excused if he is new
checks.why: Al-Tahawi says whoever hears it and claims it is human speech has disbelieved. Allah threatened such a person with Saqar.

lessons.title: What is impossible and possible for Allah
lessons.about: The opposites of His attributes, and what He freely does.

cards.x: The opposite of every necessary attribute is impossible for Allah: non-existence, having a beginning or end, resembling creation, needing anything, having a partner, weakness, ignorance, death and so on.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is impossible for Allah

cards.x: What is possible for Allah is doing or leaving anything that is possible. Nothing obliges Him: if He rewards us it is pure bounty, and if He punishes it is pure justice.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is possible for Allah; Jawharat al-Tawhid

cards.x: This protects you from two mistakes: thinking Allah is like us, and thinking anything is forced upon Him.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is possible for Allah

checks.q: Which of these is impossible for Allah?
checks.why: Needing is the opposite of 'standing by Himself', so it is impossible for Him.

checks.q: What is possible (ja'iz) for Allah, according to al-Sanusi?
checks.a: Doing or leaving anything that is possible
w: Only what is best for creation
checks.why: He may create or not create, give or withhold. Nothing forces Him.

checks.q: Is Allah obliged to reward people for good deeds?
checks.a: No, His reward is pure bounty
w: Yes, He must reward every good deed
Yes, but only the deeds done in prayer
Only the Prophets must be rewarded
checks.why: Nothing is obligatory upon Allah. He promised reward out of generosity, and He keeps His promise.

checks.q: Allah punishes someone for their sins. Is that unjust?
checks.why: If He rewards it is bounty; if He punishes it is justice. Nothing He does is wrong.

lessons.title: The Messengers عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ
lessons.about: What is necessary, impossible and possible for the Messengers.

cards.x: The Messengers are truthful (sidq), trustworthy (amanah) and convey everything they were commanded to convey (tabligh).

cards.ar: مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٖ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّـنَ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٗا ﴿٤٠﴾
cards.x: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah has knowledge of all things.
Lying, betraying trust, and hiding what they were commanded to convey are impossible for them.
Human things that do not lower their rank are possible for them, such as eating, sleeping, marriage and illness that is not repulsive.
Muhammad ﷺ is the last Prophet and the Messenger to all of mankind and jinn. There is no prophet after him.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Prophet ﷺ

checks.q: Which three qualities are necessary for every Messenger of Allah?
checks.a: Truthfulness, trustworthiness and conveying the message
w: Wisdom, power and never falling ill
Trustworthiness, kingship and knowing the unseen
checks.why: Sidq (truthfulness), amanah (trustworthiness) and tabligh (conveying) are necessary for them.

checks.q: Which of these human things is possible for a Messenger?
checks.why: Human things that do not lower their rank are possible for them.

checks.q: Who is the last Prophet, after whom there is no prophet?
checks.why: He ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets. 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ will return, but as a follower of his law.

checks.q: Which is impossible for a Messenger of Allah?
checks.why: The opposites of truthfulness, trustworthiness and conveying are impossible for them.

lessons.title: Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
lessons.about: Who he is, his rank, and what we owe him.

cards.x: Muhammad ﷺ son of 'Abdullah is the last Prophet and Messenger. There is no prophet after him. He was sent to all of mankind and jinn, until the end of time.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

cards.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلَـٰٓئِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ صَلُّواْ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسْلِيمًا ﴿٥٦﴾
cards.x: Truly Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with abundant peace.

cards.ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةٗ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ ﴿١٠٧﴾
cards.x: We did not send you except as a mercy to all the worlds.

cards.ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٖ ﴿٤﴾
cards.x: And truly you are of a tremendous character.

cards.ar: قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: Say: If you love Allah, follow me, and Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
He ﷺ is the master of the children of Adam and the best of all creation, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds. His greatest miracle is the Qur'an, which remains until the end of time.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

cards.x: Allah sent many prophets; we believe in them all. Twenty-five are named in the Qur'an, among them Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa and Muhammad عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ. The greatest of them are called the 'Ulu al-'Azm: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa and Muhammad.
cards.src: al-Fiqh al-Akbar, Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

cards.x: To believe him, obey him, follow his Sunnah, love him more than ourselves, our parents and children, honour him, and send blessings upon him whenever he is mentioned.

checks.q: After the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, will any new prophet come?
checks.a: No, he is the Seal of the Prophets
w: Yes, one more before the end
Yes, 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ as a new prophet with a new law
Only a prophet for the Arabs
checks.why: 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ will return, but following the law of Muhammad ﷺ.

checks.q: To whom was the Prophet ﷺ sent?
w: To the people of Makkah and Madinah
To the Jews and Christians only
checks.why: Earlier prophets were sent to their own people; he ﷺ was sent to all.

checks.q: What is the greatest miracle of the Prophet ﷺ, which remains today?
checks.why: His other miracles were seen by those present; the Qur'an remains for every generation.

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ said none of you truly believes until he loves him more than…
checks.a: His father, his child and all people
checks.why: Al-Bukhari narrated it in the Book of Faith.

checks.q: How many prophets are named in the Qur'an?
checks.why: Twenty-five are named; we believe in all the prophets, named or not.

lessons.title: Angels, Books and Messengers
lessons.about: Believing in all of them without distinction.

cards.x: We believe in the angels, the Prophets and the Books sent down to the Messengers, and we bear witness that they were upon the clear truth.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the angels and books

cards.ar: ءَامَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِن رَّبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ ءَامَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَـٰٓئِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٖ مِّن رُّسُلِهِ وَقَالُواْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ ﴿٢٨٥﴾
cards.x: The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers: 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers.'

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارٗا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهَا مَلَـٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظٞ شِدَادٞ لَّا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ ﴿٦﴾
cards.x: …angels stern and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded.
We make no distinction between any of His Messengers, and we accept all of them in what they brought.
Allah took Ibrahim عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ as His close friend and spoke to Musa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ directly. Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets and the master of the Messengers.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Prophet ﷺ

cards.x: We believe in the noble scribes whom Allah has made guardians over us, and in the Angel of Death who takes the souls.

Angels are made of light and never disobey Allah. Among them: Jibril brings revelation, Mika'il is over rain and provision, Israfil will blow the Trumpet, and the Angel of Death takes souls. The Books: the Tawrah to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, the Injil to 'Isa, and the Qur'an to Muhammad ﷺ, which is protected and comes after them all.

checks.q: How do Muslims believe in the Messengers of Allah?
checks.a: In all of them, without rejecting any
w: Only in those named in the Qur'an
In all of them, but follow only Musa's law
Only in the last one, the others are replaced
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: we make no distinction between His Messengers in believing them.

checks.q: To which Prophet did Allah speak directly, without an angel?
checks.why: 'And Allah spoke to Musa directly.' (al-Nisa' 164), quoted by al-Tahawi.

checks.q: Who are the 'noble scribes' (kiraman katibin)?
checks.a: The angels who record our deeds
w: The Companions who wrote the Qur'an
checks.why: Allah has made them guardians over us, writing what we do.

checks.q: Which Prophet did Allah take as His close friend (khalil)?
checks.why: 'And Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend.' (al-Nisa' 125), quoted by al-Tahawi.

checks.q: Which Book was given to 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ?
checks.why: Tawrah to Musa, Zabur to Dawud, Injil to 'Isa, Qur'an to Muhammad ﷺ.

lessons.title: The meaning of the Shahadah
lessons.about: How 'la ilaha illa Allah' gathers all of belief.

cards.x: Imam al-Sanusi ends by showing that all of belief is gathered in 'La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammadun Rasulullah'.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

cards.ar: فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنبِكَ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكُمْ وَمَثْوَىٰكُمْ ﴿١٩﴾
cards.x: So know that there is no god but Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin.
Its meaning: there is none who is free of need of everything else, and whom everything else needs, except Allah. Every attribute we learnt follows from this.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

cards.x: 'Muhammadun Rasulullah' brings in belief in all the Prophets and angels, the books and the Last Day, because he ﷺ came with all of it. So say it often, knowing what it means.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

checks.q: Al-Sanusi explains 'la ilaha illa Allah' (no god but Allah). What does it mean?
checks.a: None is free of need of all else, and needed by all, except Allah
w: Allah is the greatest of many beings we worship
None deserves to be called great except Allah
Allah is present in every place and thing
checks.why: Every attribute of Allah follows from this: He needs nothing, and everything needs Him.

checks.q: Belief in the angels and the Last Day is contained in which half of the Shahadah?
checks.a: 'Muhammadun Rasulullah' (Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah)
w: 'La ilaha illa Allah' (there is no god but Allah)
Neither half: it is learnt separately
Both halves equally, word for word
checks.why: Accepting the Messenger ﷺ means accepting everything he brought, including the angels, the books and the Last Day.

checks.q: How does al-Sanusi advise us to say the Shahadah?
w: Once in your life, with full meaning
Silently, and leave its meaning to scholars
checks.why: He closes the book urging the believer to say it often with awareness of its meaning.

checks.q: Why should we know the meaning of 'la ilaha illa Allah', not only say it?
checks.a: Because every belief about Allah follows from its meaning
w: Because the words alone have no reward
Because only scholars may say it
Because it must be translated before it is said
checks.why: Al-Sanusi shows that all the attributes are contained in it, so knowing it strengthens faith.

lessons.title: What a believer believes
lessons.about: The articles of faith, what faith is, and love of the Companions.

cards.x: A believer believes in Allah, His angels, His books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and that good and bad are by Allah's decree.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

cards.x: Faith (iman) is affirming with the tongue and believing with the heart everything the Prophet ﷺ brought from Allah.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

cards.x: We love the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We do not go to excess in loving any one of them, and we do not disown any of them. We mention them only with good.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

checks.q: How does Imam al-Tahawi define faith (iman)?
checks.a: Affirming with the tongue and believing with the heart
w: Doing good deeds, with or without belief
Believing in the heart, with no need to say it
Saying it with the tongue, with no need to believe
checks.why: Faith is believing in the heart and declaring with the tongue all the Prophet ﷺ brought.

checks.q: Which of these is one of the six articles of faith?
checks.a: Belief in Allah's decree, the good and the bad
w: Belief that the stars decide events
Belief in lucky and unlucky days
Belief that the saints are prophets
checks.why: The six: Allah, His angels, books, Messengers, the Last Day, and the decree.

checks.q: How do we speak about the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ?
checks.a: Only with good, without going to excess about any
w: Praise the best and keep quiet about the rest
checks.why: We love them all, go to excess with none, disown none, and mention them only with good.

checks.q: Who are the Companions (Sahabah)?
checks.a: Muslims who met him ﷺ and died Muslim
w: Only the people of his house
checks.why: We love them all and speak of them only with good.

lessons.title: Sin, faith and hope
lessons.about: A sin does not take a believer out of Islam.

cards.x: We do not declare anyone of the people of the qiblah a disbeliever for a sin, as long as he does not hold it to be lawful.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on sin and faith

cards.ar: قُلْ يَٰعِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُواْ مِن رَّحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿٥٣﴾
cards.x: Say: O My servants who have wronged themselves, do not despair of Allah's mercy. Truly Allah forgives all sins. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

Those of the Ummah who commit major sins will not be in the Fire forever if they die believing in Allah's Oneness. They are in His will: if He wills He forgives them, and if He wills He punishes them by His justice.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the people of major sins

cards.x: We hope for the good-doers and fear for the wrongdoers, without despairing for them. Feeling safe from Allah and despairing of Him both take one away from Islam; the path of truth is between them.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on sin and faith

checks.q: A Muslim commits a sin. Does that make him a disbeliever?
checks.a: No, unless he claims the sin is lawful
w: Yes, any major sin takes him out of Islam
Only if he repeats the sin many times
Only if he does not pray
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: we do not call anyone of the qiblah a disbeliever for a sin, unless he holds it lawful.

checks.q: A believer dies with major sins he did not repent from. What is his state?
checks.a: He is under Allah's will, and will not stay in the Fire forever
w: He will stay in the Fire forever
He is certainly forgiven, without any punishment
He was never a believer to begin with
checks.why: If Allah wills He forgives him; if He wills He punishes him, then admits him to Paradise.

checks.q: Between feeling safe from Allah's punishment and despairing of His mercy, where is the right path?
checks.why: Both extremes take a person away from Islam. The believer hopes and fears.

checks.q: A believer commits a major sin. Can repentance (tawbah) wipe it out?
w: No, only minor sins can be forgiven
checks.why: Allah forgives all sins for the one who repents sincerely, before death or the sun rising from the west.

lessons.title: What takes a person out of Islam
lessons.about: Guarding your faith: what is disbelief, and how to return.

cards.x: Iman can be lost. The scholars teach every Muslim what takes a person out of Islam, so they can guard their faith, just as they guard their prayer.
cards.src: al-Fiqh al-Akbar, What takes a person out of Islam

cards.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّمَا كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ قُلْ أَبِاللَّهِ وَءَايَٰتِهِ وَرَسُولِهِ كُنتُمْ تَسْتَهْزِءُونَ ﴿٦٥﴾ لَا تَعْتَذِرُواْ قَدْ كَفَرْتُم بَعْدَ إِيمَٰنِكُمْ إِن نَّعْفُ عَن طَآئِفَةٖ مِّنكُمْ نُعَذِّبْ طَآئِفَةَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ مُجْرِمِينَ ﴿٦٦﴾
cards.x: If you ask them, they will say: 'We were only chatting and joking.' Say: 'Was it Allah, His signs and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuses: you have disbelieved after your belief.'

Doubting Allah, the Prophet ﷺ or the Qur'an; believing Allah has a partner, a body or a child; or denying something every Muslim knows is part of the religion, such as the prayer being fard or alcohol being haram.
cards.src: al-Fiqh al-Akbar, What takes a person out of Islam

cards.x: Mocking Allah, His Messenger ﷺ, the Qur'an or the religion, even as a joke; and deeds that only mean disbelief, such as prostrating to an idol or throwing the Qur'an in filth.
cards.src: al-Fiqh al-Akbar, What takes a person out of Islam

cards.x: Whoever falls into this must repent at once and say the Shahadah again sincerely. Allah accepts the one who returns. But we do not call any Muslim a disbeliever ourselves; that is for qualified scholars, with great caution.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, What takes a person out of Islam

checks.q: Someone mocks the prayer as a joke. What is the ruling?
checks.a: It is disbelief, even as a joke
w: It is fine if no one was offended
checks.why: Mocking any part of the religion, even jokingly, takes a person out of Islam. Repent and renew the Shahadah.

checks.q: A Muslim drinks alcohol but believes it is haram. Is he a disbeliever?
checks.a: No, he is a sinful believer
w: Yes, unless he drinks only a little
Only if he does it in public
checks.why: Committing a sin is not disbelief. Claiming it is lawful would be.

checks.q: Someone realises they said words of disbelief. What should they do?
checks.a: Repent at once and say the Shahadah again
checks.why: Return immediately and sincerely; Allah accepts the one who turns back.

checks.q: May an ordinary Muslim declare another Muslim a disbeliever?
checks.a: No; it is for qualified scholars, with great caution
w: Yes, if he disagrees with us
Yes, if he misses a prayer
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: we do not call anyone of the qiblah a disbeliever for a sin.

lessons.title: Shirk: the sin Allah does not forgive
lessons.about: What shirk is, the hidden kind, and how to stay clear of it.

cards.x: Shirk is believing anyone shares in Allah's divinity: that another creates, deserves worship, or has power of its own besides Him. Allah forgives everything except dying upon shirk.

cards.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ افْتَرَىٰٓ إِثْمًا عَظِيمًا ﴿٤٨﴾
cards.x: Truly Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives anything less than that to whom He wills.

cards.ar: وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَٰنُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَٰبُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٞ ﴿١٣﴾
cards.x: Luqman said to his son, advising him: 'My son, do not associate partners with Allah. Truly, associating partners is a tremendous wrong.'
Riya', doing good deeds to be seen by people, is called the lesser or hidden shirk. It does not take you out of Islam, but it spoils the deed.
Believing that charms, stars, unlucky numbers or days bring good or harm by themselves contradicts tawhid. Everything happens only by Allah's will.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Shirk: the sin Allah does not forgive

cards.x: Asking Allah by the rank of the Prophet ﷺ or the righteous (tawassul), visiting graves and greeting the dead, and asking the righteous to make du'a for you are the way of Ahl al-Sunnah, as long as you believe only Allah creates benefit and harm. Calling Muslims mushriks for these is a grave error.

checks.q: Which sin does Allah not forgive if a person dies upon it?
checks.why: 'Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but forgives anything less than that for whom He wills.' (al-Nisa' 48)

checks.q: Praying so that people praise you is called…
checks.why: It spoils the deed but does not take you out of Islam. Fix your intention.

checks.q: Someone believes a lucky charm protects them by its own power. What does it contradict?
checks.a: Tawhid: only Allah brings benefit and harm
checks.why: Benefit and harm come only from Allah.

checks.q: Someone says 'O Allah, I ask You by the rank of Your Prophet ﷺ'. What is this?
checks.why: Asking Allah alone, through someone beloved to Him, is not worship of other than Allah.

lessons.title: The grave and the Last Day
lessons.about: What al-Tahawi tells us to believe about what comes after death.

cards.x: We believe in the punishment of the grave for those who deserve it, and in the questioning by Munkar and Nakir about one's Lord, religion and Prophet. The grave is a garden of Paradise or a pit of the Fire.

cards.ar: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرٗا يَرَهُ ﴿٧﴾ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٖ شَرّٗا يَرَهُ ﴿٨﴾
cards.x: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.

cards.ar: وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَٰزِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٞ شَيْـٔٗا وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٖ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ ﴿٤٧﴾
cards.x: We will set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in the least.

We believe in the resurrection, the recompense of deeds on the Day of Judgement, the presenting of records, the reckoning, the reading of the book, the reward and punishment, the Bridge and the Scales.
The Pool (hawd) with which Allah honoured the Prophet ﷺ, to quench his Ummah, is true. The intercession he has stored for them is true.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the Pool and the intercession

cards.x: Paradise and the Fire are created. They will never end and never perish.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Paradise and the Fire

checks.q: Which two angels question a person in the grave?
checks.why: They ask about one's Lord, religion and Prophet. The grave is a garden of Paradise or a pit of the Fire.

checks.q: What does Imam al-Tahawi say about Paradise and the Fire?
checks.a: They already exist and will never end
w: They will be created on the Last Day
They exist now, but will end after a long time
Only Paradise exists now and lasts forever
checks.why: They are created now, and they never end or perish.

checks.q: What is the Pool (hawd) of the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Judgement?
checks.a: A real pool from which he gives his Ummah to drink
w: A symbol of his mercy, not a real pool
A pool for the Prophets alone
A pool in Madinah in this world
checks.why: It is an honour Allah gave him ﷺ, to quench the thirst of his Ummah.

checks.q: On the Day of Judgement, what is the Sirat?
checks.a: The Bridge over the Fire that people cross
w: The Scale on which deeds are weighed
The gate that leads into Paradise
The river of al-Kawthar in Paradise
checks.why: Al-Tahawi lists the Bridge with the Scales, the reckoning and the books of deeds.

lessons.title: Seeing Allah in Paradise
lessons.about: A truth for the people of Paradise, without 'how'.

cards.x: The believers will see Allah in Paradise, without encompassing Him and without asking how. 'Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord.' (al-Qiyamah 22–23)
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the seeing of Allah

cards.ar: وُجُوهٞ يَوْمَئِذٖ نَّاضِرَةٌ ﴿٢٢﴾ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٞ ﴿٢٣﴾
cards.x: Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord.

Imam al-Tahawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says the meaning of seeing Allah is as Allah intended and knows. The sound hadith say the believers will see their Lord as clearly as the full moon. We accept these as the Prophet ﷺ said them, without picturing how and without comparing Allah to creation.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the seeing of Allah

cards.x: No one's religion is safe except the one who submits to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and leaves what is unclear to the One who knows it.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the seeing of Allah

checks.q: Will the believers see Allah in Paradise?
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: the seeing is true for the people of Paradise, without encompassing Him and without 'how'.

checks.q: Which verse does Imam al-Tahawi quote as proof that believers will see Allah?
checks.a: 'Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord'
w: 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing'
'Say: He is Allah, One; Allah, the Self-Sufficient'
'Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth'
checks.why: Al-Qiyamah 22–23 speaks of faces on the Day of Judgement looking at their Lord.

checks.q: How do we understand the hadith that say believers will see Allah?
checks.a: As the Prophet ﷺ said them, meant as Allah intends
w: As our reason tells us, picturing how
As pictures, comparing Allah to creation
We reject them, since Allah is not seen
checks.why: We accept them, without imagining how and without likening Allah to anything.

checks.q: Imam al-Tahawi says nobody's religion is safe except…
checks.a: The one who submits to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ
w: The one who argues for his belief best
The one who studies the philosophers
The one who asks no questions at all
checks.why: Submitting, and leaving what is unclear to the One who knows it, keeps religion safe.

lessons.title: Allah's decree (qadr)
lessons.about: Everything happens by His knowledge and will.

cards.x: Qadr (decree) means Allah knew everything before it happened, wrote it, and nothing happens in His kingdom except what He wills, good or bad.

cards.ar: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَٰهُ بِقَدَرٖ ﴿٤٩﴾
cards.x: Truly, We have created everything according to a measure.

cards.ar: وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿٩٦﴾
cards.x: When Allah has created you and what you do.
The decree is Allah's secret in His creation. No angel near to Him nor Prophet sent has been shown it. Looking too deeply into it leads to ruin.
Our actions are created by Allah and earned (kasb) by us. So we act, we take responsibility, and we trust Him.

checks.q: Can anything happen in creation that Allah did not will?
checks.a: No, only what He wills happens
w: Only good things are His will
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: nothing happens in His kingdom except what He wills.

checks.q: What does Imam al-Tahawi say about digging deep into the secret of qadr (decree)?
checks.a: It is Allah's secret; delving into it leads to ruin
w: Every Muslim must study it in detail
It is easy to understand with reason
Only the Prophets may ask about it
checks.why: No angel or Prophet has been shown it. We believe in it and act.

checks.q: If Allah has decreed everything, how are we responsible for our actions?
checks.a: Allah creates our actions and we earn (kasb) them by choosing
w: We create our own actions, so Allah does not
We are forced, so we are not responsible
Allah only learns of them when we do them
checks.why: We choose and are accountable, while Allah creates. So we act, take responsibility, and trust Him.

checks.q: Something bad happens to you. What does belief in qadr (decree) teach?
checks.a: It was decreed by Allah; be patient and trust Him
w: It happened by chance; nothing could be done
Allah did not know about it until it happened
The evil eye alone caused it, not Allah
checks.why: Good and bad are by Allah's decree. The believer is grateful in ease and patient in hardship.

lessons.title: Using the toilet and istinja'
lessons.about: Cleaning yourself properly, and the manners of the toilet.

cards.x: Istinja' means cleaning the private parts after using the toilet, with water or with something like stones or tissue. Istibra' means making sure the urine has completely stopped before cleaning. Najasah means impurity, such as urine or faeces.

A man must make sure the last drops of urine have stopped before he cleans himself and makes wudu, in whatever way works for him, such as walking a little, coughing or waiting. If drops come out after wudu, the wudu breaks.
A woman does not need the man's istibra'. She waits a moment until the flow has stopped, then cleans herself. She should wipe and wash from front to back, so that impurity is not carried forward.

Istinja' is a sunnah. Wiping with clean stones (or tissue) is allowed, washing with water is better, and the best is to wipe first and then wash. If impurity spreads beyond the opening more than the size of a dirham (about the hollow of the palm), washing it becomes fard.

cards.x: Enter with the left foot, seeking refuge in Allah from Shaytan before going in, and leave with the right foot saying: 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi adhhaba 'anni al-adha wa 'afani.'

lessons.title: Impurities and what is excused
lessons.about: Heavy and light impurity, and how much prevents prayer.

cards.x: A dirham was a silver coin. In this chapter it is a measure. For liquid impurity it is an area: the hollow of your palm when you cup it, roughly 3 cm across, about the size of a 2p coin. For solid impurity it is a weight of 20 qirats (a mithqal), a few grams.
Heavy (ghalizah) impurities include wine, flowing blood, urine of animals that are not eaten, dog and predator droppings, and anything from the human body that breaks wudu when it comes out.
Light (khafifah) impurities include the urine of a horse or of animals that are eaten, and droppings of birds that are not eaten.

'Excused' means the prayer is still valid, not that you may leave it. Heavy impurity: less than a dirham, the prayer is valid but washing it is sunnah; exactly a dirham, washing it is wajib and praying with it is strongly disliked; more than a dirham, it must be washed or the prayer is invalid. Light impurity: excused if less than a quarter of the garment or limb. Tiny pinhead splashes of urine are excused.

cards.x: Tayammum is purifying with clean earth when water cannot be used. It is allowed when you are a mile or more from water (a Hanafi mile is about 1.8 km), when using water would make you ill or worse, when it is dangerously cold, or when you need the water to drink.

cards.x: …and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands. Truly Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving.

Make the intention (in tayammum it is fard, unlike wudu), strike clean earth with both palms and wipe the whole face; strike again and wipe both arms including the elbows. Remove or move rings so nothing is left unwiped.
Tayammum stands in place of wudu and ghusl. It ends when water becomes available and you are able to use it.

checks.q: What is tayammum?
checks.a: Purifying with clean earth when water can't be used
w: Making wudu with very little water
Wiping over socks instead of washing
Washing only the face and hands
checks.why: Tayammum stands in place of wudu and ghusl when water cannot be used.

checks.q: You can't find water. How far away must it be for tayammum to be allowed?
checks.a: A mile or more, about 1.8 km
w: Any distance, if you are tired
checks.why: A Hanafi mile is 4,000 cubits, about 1.8 km.

checks.q: In tayammum, how many times are the hands struck on the earth?
checks.a: Twice: once for the face, once for the arms
w: Once: for the face and arms together
Three times: face, arms, then feet
Twice: once for the face, once for the feet
checks.why: Strike, wipe the face; strike again, wipe both arms with the elbows.

checks.q: What ends tayammum, besides what breaks wudu?
checks.a: Finding water you are able to use
w: The next prayer time coming in
Nothing ends it until you sleep
checks.why: It stands in place of water only until water can be used.

lessons.title: Wiping over leather socks (khuffs)
lessons.about: When you may wipe, for how long, and how.

cards.x: Khuffs are leather socks that cover the ankles. If you put them on while in wudu, then later make wudu again, you may wipe over them with wet hands instead of washing your feet, for a set time.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the time limit for wiping

cards.x: A resident wipes for one day and night, a traveller for three days and nights. The time starts from the first thing that breaks wudu after putting them on.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the time limit for wiping

cards.x: Put them on after washing the feet, in wudu. They must cover the ankles, be strong enough to walk in, and have no hole the size of three small toes.
The fard is wiping the top of the front of each foot, the size of three of the hand's small fingers. The sunnah is drawing spread fingers from the toes up towards the shin.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the amount that is fard

checks.q: What are khuffs?
w: A cloth wrapped round the feet
checks.why: If put on while in wudu, you may wipe over them instead of washing your feet, for a set time.

checks.q: How long may a traveller wipe over leather socks (khuffs)?
checks.why: A resident wipes one day and night; a traveller three.

checks.q: When wiping over leather socks (khuffs), when does the time limit start?
checks.a: From the first thing that breaks wudu after wearing them
w: From the moment you put them on in wudu
From the next Fajr after putting them on
From the first time you wipe over them
checks.why: Put them on in wudu at Fajr, and your wudu breaks at noon: the count starts at noon.

checks.q: When wiping over leather socks (khuffs), what is the least you must wipe?
checks.a: Three fingers' width on the top of each foot
w: The whole sock, top and bottom
checks.why: The fard is the size of three of the hand's small fingers on the top front of each foot.

lessons.title: Menstruation and post-natal bleeding
lessons.about: Its length and what is not allowed during it.

cards.x: Hayd is menstruation, the monthly period. Nifas is the bleeding after giving birth. The shortest hayd is three days and the longest ten. Nifas is at most forty days, with no minimum: it can end after a day.
During menstruation and nifas: prayer, fasting, reciting a verse of the Qur'an, touching the Qur'an without a cover, entering a masjid, tawaf, and intercourse.
She makes up the fasts she missed, but not the prayers.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, making up the obligations

cards.x: Bleeding shorter than three days, longer than ten, or beyond forty after birth is istihadah (irregular bleeding). It does not stop prayer or fasting: she makes wudu for each prayer time and prays.

checks.q: What is nifas?
w: Bleeding from a cut or wound
checks.why: Nifas is post-natal bleeding. Hayd is the monthly period.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, what is the longest a period (hayd) can last?
checks.why: The shortest hayd is three days and the longest ten. Bleeding beyond that is not hayd.

checks.q: What is the longest nifas (bleeding after giving birth) can last?
checks.why: Nifas is at most forty days, with no minimum: it may end after a day.

checks.q: After her period, what does a woman make up?
checks.why: She makes up missed fasts. Missed prayers are forgiven, a mercy from Allah.

lessons.title: Constant bleeding, wounds and casts
lessons.about: For anyone with a flow they cannot stop, or a dressing they cannot remove.

cards.x: Someone with a constant flow that breaks wudu, such as drops of urine, wind, a bleeding wound or irregular bleeding (istihadah), is excused (ma'dhur) once it continues through a whole prayer time without a break long enough to make wudu and pray the fard.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, when an excuse is established

cards.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَآ إِصْرٗا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَآ أَنتَ مَوْلَىٰنَا فَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَٰفِرِينَ ﴿٢٨٦﴾
cards.x: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.

They make wudu once the prayer time has begun, and pray with it every fard and voluntary prayer they wish in that time. That flow does not break it, though anything else does. When the time ends, the wudu ends.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of istihadah and similar cases

cards.x: Once established, the excuse continues as long as the flow appears at least once in each later prayer time. If a whole prayer time passes without it, the person is no longer excused.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, when an excuse is established

cards.x: If a limb has a cast, splint or dressing and washing it or taking it off would cause harm, wipe once over most of it with a wet hand in wudu or ghusl, and wash the rest. It has no time limit and need not be put on in wudu.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, splints and the like

cards.x: Women's bleeding has detailed rulings built on each woman's habit. Note the start and end of every period and every bleeding, and ask a qualified teacher when it is irregular.

checks.q: Drops of urine come throughout every prayer time. With one wudu, the person may pray…
checks.a: Every prayer they wish until that time ends
checks.why: The flow they are excused for does not break their wudu until the time ends.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of istihadah and similar cases

checks.q: Your arm is in a cast and washing it would harm you. In wudu you…
checks.a: Wipe over most of the cast and wash the rest
w: Do tayammum for the whole wudu
Leave the arm and pray anyway
checks.why: Wiping over a splint or dressing stands in place of washing beneath it.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, splints and the like

checks.q: When does an excused person's wudu end?
checks.a: When the prayer time ends, or something else breaks it
checks.why: A new time needs a new wudu.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of istihadah and similar cases

lessons.title: The five prayer times
lessons.about: When each prayer starts and ends, and the forbidden times.

cards.x: Fajr is from true dawn (when light spreads across the horizon) until just before sunrise. Zuhr is from when the sun passes its highest point until an object's shadow is twice its length (once, in the view of the two companions), not counting its midday shadow.

cards.ar: فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ الصَّلَوٰةَ فَاذْكُرُواْ اللَّهَ قِيَٰمٗا وَقُعُودٗا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِكُمْ فَإِذَا اطْمَأْنَنتُمْ فَأَقِيمُواْ الصَّلَوٰةَ إِنَّ الصَّلَوٰةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَٰبٗا مَّوْقُوتٗا ﴿١٠٣﴾
cards.x: Truly, the prayer is prescribed for the believers at set times.

cards.ar: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى الصَّلَوَٰتِ وَالصَّلَوٰةِ الْوُسْطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ ﴿٢٣٨﴾
cards.x: Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion.
'Asr is from the end of Zuhr until sunset. Maghrib is from sunset until the red twilight disappears. 'Isha' and witr are from then until dawn; witr is not prayed before 'Isha'.

No prayer is valid at sunrise until the sun has risen, or when it is at its height. When the sun turns yellow before setting, no prayer is valid except that same day's 'Asr: if you have not prayed it, pray it then, though delaying it that late is sinful. Voluntary prayer is also disliked after the Fajr prayer until sunrise, and after the 'Asr prayer until sunset.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the times when prayer is not valid

checks.q: When does the time of Fajr end?
w: At the first light of dawn
checks.why: Fajr lasts from true dawn until just before the sun rises.

checks.q: When does Maghrib end in the Hanafi fatwa?
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: until the red twilight is gone, on the view the fatwa follows.

checks.q: Which is a time when prayer is not valid?
w: In the middle of the night
checks.why: Sunrise, the sun's height and its setting are the three forbidden times.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the times when prayer is not valid

checks.q: When does the time of Maghrib end?
checks.why: Maghrib lasts from sunset until the redness in the sky has gone; then 'Isha' begins.

checks.q: You have not prayed 'Asr and the sun is turning yellow. What do you do?
checks.a: Pray it now; that day's 'Asr is still valid
w: Wait and make it up after Maghrib
Leave it, it is a forbidden time
checks.why: Today's 'Asr is the exception. Pray it, and repent for delaying it so late.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, The five prayer times

lessons.title: The adhan and iqamah
lessons.about: Their ruling and their words.

cards.x: The adhan and iqamah are a stressed sunnah for every fard prayer, for men, whether praying alone or in a group, at home or travelling, on time or making up.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of the adhan and iqamah

cards.x: Say 'Allahu akbar' four times at the start, then each phrase twice, ending with 'Allahu akbar' twice and 'La ilaha illa Allah'. The iqamah is the same.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the adhan is given

cards.x: Allahu akbar: Allah is the Greatest. Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah: I bear witness there is no god but Allah. Ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah: I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Hayya 'ala al-salah: come to prayer. Hayya 'ala al-falah: come to success. La ilaha illa Allah: there is no god but Allah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of the adhan and iqamah

cards.x: In the adhan of Fajr add 'al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm' (prayer is better than sleep) twice after 'hayya 'ala al-falah'. In the iqamah add 'qad qamat al-salah' (the prayer has begun) twice. Give the adhan slowly and the iqamah quickly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the adhan is given

checks.q: What does 'hayya 'ala al-falah' in the adhan mean?
checks.why: 'Hayya 'ala al-salah' is 'come to prayer'; 'hayya 'ala al-falah' is 'come to success'.

checks.q: What is the ruling of the adhan for a fard prayer?
checks.why: A stressed sunnah for every fard prayer, for men.

checks.q: In the adhan of Fajr, what is added, and what does it mean?
checks.a: 'Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm': prayer is better than sleep
w: 'Qad qamat al-salah': the prayer has begun
'Hayya 'ala al-falah': come to success, said four times
'Allahu akbar': Allah is the Greatest, said six times
checks.why: It is said twice after 'hayya 'ala al-falah', reminding the sleeper.

checks.q: What is added in the iqamah, and what does it mean?
checks.a: 'Qad qamat al-salah': the prayer has begun
checks.why: The iqamah is said just before the prayer starts, and said quickly.

lessons.title: Before you pray
lessons.about: The conditions that must be in place before your prayer starts.

cards.x: You must be in wudu (and ghusl if needed), and your body, clothes and the place you pray on must be clean of impurity.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: The 'awrah is the part of the body that must be covered. In prayer, for a man it is from the navel to the knees, the knees included. For a woman it is the whole body except the face, the hands and the feet.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: Face the qiblah, pray after the time has come in, and intend the prayer you are praying, such as today's Zuhr.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: Begin with 'Allahu akbar' while standing, saying it so that you hear yourself.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

checks.q: In prayer, the 'awrah (what must be covered) for a man is…
checks.a: From the navel to below the knees
w: From the chest to the ankles
The whole body except the face
checks.why: A man's 'awrah is from the navel to below the knees; a woman's is all but the face, hands and feet.

checks.q: You pray Zuhr before its time has come in. Is it valid?
checks.a: No, the time must have come in
w: Yes, if you did not know
checks.why: A prayer before its time is not valid; pray it again once the time comes in.

checks.q: Which of these is a condition for the prayer to be valid?
checks.a: A clean body, clothes and place
w: Praying in a masjid, in congregation
Praying at the start of the time
checks.why: Purity of body, clothes and place, covering the 'awrah, facing the qiblah, the time and the intention.

lessons.title: The pillars of prayer

cards.x: Inside the prayer, four things are pillars: standing, reciting, bowing (ruku') and prostrating (sujud).
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

cards.x: Nur al-Idah names these four, then adds that the final sitting, for as long as it takes to recite the tashahhud, is also said to be a pillar. Either way it is fard: the prayer is not valid without it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

cards.x: If a pillar is missed, the prayer is not valid and must be prayed again. The prostration of forgetfulness cannot fix it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

checks.q: Which of these is a pillar (fard part) inside the prayer?
w: Placing the right hand over the left

checks.q: You missed a pillar of the prayer, like a sujud. What do you do?
checks.a: Pray it again; it is not valid
w: Two prostrations of forgetfulness fix it

checks.q: How long must the final sitting of the prayer be, at least?
checks.why: The final sitting is fard for at least the length of the tashahhud.

lessons.title: The wajib acts of prayer
lessons.about: The wajib acts, and what to do if you miss one.

cards.x: Wajib acts include: reciting al-Fatihah, adding a surah or three verses, calmness in every position, the first sitting, the tashahhud, and ending with 'al-salam'.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

cards.x: If you leave a wajib act by mistake, make two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) at the end, with tashahhud and salam.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

cards.x: If you leave a wajib act deliberately, you are sinful and must repeat the prayer.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, reciting al-Fatihah is…

checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: You forgot the first sitting. What do you do?
checks.a: Make the two prostrations of forgetfulness at the end
w: Start the prayer again straight away
checks.why: The first sitting is wajib. Leaving it by mistake is fixed with two prostrations of forgetfulness at the end.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: You left a wajib act on purpose. What follows?
checks.a: You are sinful and must repeat the prayer
w: Two prostrations of forgetfulness fix it
Nothing, if it was a small act
checks.why: Leaving a wajib act on purpose is sinful, and the prayer must be repeated.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: Which of these is wajib in prayer, not a pillar?
checks.why: In the Hanafi school reciting is a pillar, but al-Fatihah in particular is wajib.

lessons.title: How to pray (1): from takbir to ruku'
lessons.about: The prayer step by step, as Nur al-Idah describes it.

cards.x: Raise the hands to the ears (a woman to her shoulders) and say 'Allahu akbar', intending the prayer. A man places his right hand over his left below the navel; a woman places them on her chest.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.ar: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿١﴾ الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَٰشِعُونَ ﴿٢﴾
cards.x: Successful indeed are the believers: those who are humble in their prayer.
Say the opening praise: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bi-hamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk.' Then seek refuge (a'udhu billah) and say bismillah quietly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Recite al-Fatihah, say 'amin' quietly, then a surah or three verses.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Say 'Allahu akbar' and bow, back straight with the head level with it, holding the knees with fingers spread. Say 'Subhana rabbiya al-'azim' three times, the least of the sunnah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

checks.q: Where does a man place his hands after the takbir?
checks.a: Right over left, below the navel
w: Right over left, on the chest
Left over right, below the navel
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: right over left below the navel for a man; a woman places them on her chest.

checks.q: What is said straight after the opening takbir?
checks.why: The opening praise (thana') comes first, then ta'awwudh and bismillah.

checks.q: How many times is the tasbih of ruku' said at least, by the sunnah?
checks.why: Three times is the least of the sunnah.

checks.q: Where does a man place his hands while standing in prayer?
checks.a: Right over left, below the navel
w: Right over left, on the chest
Left over right, on the chest
checks.why: A man places them below the navel; a woman places them on her chest.

lessons.title: How to pray (2): from rising to salam
lessons.about: Prostration, sitting, tashahhud and ending the prayer.

cards.x: Rise saying 'Sami' Allahu li-man hamidah, rabbana laka al-hamd' (a follower says only the second part), and stand still for a moment.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Go down with 'Allahu akbar', placing knees, then hands, then face between the hands, nose and forehead on the ground. Say 'Subhana rabbiya al-a'la' three times. Sit calmly, then make the second sujud the same way.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: After the second rak'ah, sit on the left foot with the right foot upright, hands on the thighs, and recite the tashahhud: 'Al-tahiyyatu lillahi wa al-salawatu wa al-tayyibat…'

In the final sitting, after the tashahhud send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ and make du'a in words like the Qur'an and the reported supplications. Then say 'al-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah' to the right and to the left.

A woman raises her hands to her shoulders, places them on her chest, bows less deeply, and in sujud keeps her body together, stomach close to her thighs and arms on the ground. In the sitting she sits with both feet out to the right side. She recites quietly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, How to pray (2): from rising to salam

checks.q: Which touches the ground first when going into sujud?
checks.why: Knees, then hands, then the face.

checks.q: What does a follower say when rising from ruku'?
checks.why: The imam or one praying alone says both; the follower says only the praise.

checks.q: What comes after the tashahhud in the final sitting?
checks.a: Blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then du'a, then salam
w: Salam straight away, then du'a afterwards
Du'a, then blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then salam
Another sujud, then blessings, then salam
checks.why: Al-Quduri: tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, du'a, then salam right and left.

checks.q: What is said three times in sujud?
checks.why: 'Subhana rabbiya al-a'la' (glory to my Lord, the Most High) in sujud; 'al-'azim' (the Magnificent) is said in ruku'.

checks.q: How does a woman sit in the tashahhud?
checks.a: Both feet out to the right side, sitting on the ground
w: On her left foot with the right upright
checks.why: A man sits on his left foot with the right upright; a woman sits with both feet out to the right.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, How to pray (2): from rising to salam

lessons.title: The five prayers, rak'ah by rak'ah
lessons.about: How many rak'ahs each prayer has, and how a whole prayer flows.

cards.x: Fard: Fajr 2, Zuhr 4, 'Asr 4, Maghrib 3, 'Isha' 4, and Jumu'ah 2 in place of Zuhr on Friday. Witr is 3 after 'Isha'. The imam recites aloud in Fajr, Jumu'ah, and the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and 'Isha'; the rest is quiet.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, The five prayers, rak'ah by rak'ah

cards.x: Takbir, opening praise, al-Fatihah and a surah, ruku', standing, two sujud: that is one rak'ah. Stand and do the same again without the opening praise, then sit for the tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, du'a and salam.

lessons.title: Praying in congregation
lessons.about: Its ruling, who leads, and following the imam.

cards.x: Praying in congregation is a stressed sunnah.
The most entitled to lead is the one who knows the sunnah best; if equal, the best reciter; then the most scrupulous; then the oldest.
Whoever joins another's prayer needs two intentions: the prayer itself and following the imam. In the Hanafi school the follower does not recite behind the imam.

If you join while the imam is in ruku' and bow before he rises, you have caught that rak'ah. If you join after he rises, that rak'ah is not counted. Do not give salam with the imam: when he finishes, stand and make up the rak'ahs you missed. A traveller behind a resident imam prays four.
