checks.q: What happens to a prayer that was missed?
checks.a: It stays owed and must be made up
w: It is forgiven if you repent
It is dropped after a year
checks.why: Make it up, and repent if it was missed deliberately.

lessons.title: The Jumu'ah prayer
lessons.about: Who must attend, and the khutbah.

cards.x: Jumu'ah is fard on a man who is free, resident in a town, healthy, safe, able to see and able to walk.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Jumu'ah: conditions of obligation

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ الْبَيْعَ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٞ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ ﴿٩﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, when the call is made for the prayer on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if only you knew.

Its sunnahs include purity, standing, facing the people, beginning with praise of Allah, the two testimonies, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, admonition, reciting a verse, and two khutbahs with a sitting between them.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the khutbah and its sunnahs

cards.x: Women and travellers do not have to attend. If someone not obliged attends and prays it, it counts in place of Zuhr.

Jumu'ah replaces Zuhr for that day. Once the imam comes out for the khutbah, there is no voluntary prayer and no talking: listen in silence, even if you cannot hear. Even telling someone 'be quiet' is not allowed.

checks.q: Is Jumu'ah fard on a traveller?
checks.why: Residence is one of its conditions of obligation.

checks.q: How many khutbahs are given, by the sunnah?
checks.a: Two, with a sitting between them
checks.why: Two khutbahs with a sitting in between are among its sunnahs.

checks.q: A woman attends Jumu'ah and prays it. Then…
checks.a: It counts in place of Zuhr
checks.why: If those not obliged attend and pray it, it is valid for them in place of Zuhr.

checks.q: Who must attend Jumu'ah?
checks.a: A free, resident, healthy adult Muslim man
w: Only those living near a masjid
checks.why: Women, travellers and the ill are excused; if they attend, it counts in place of Zuhr.

lessons.title: The funeral prayer
lessons.about: Its ruling, conditions and how it is prayed.

cards.x: Praying over a Muslim who has died is fard kifayah: if some pray it, the rest are excused. Its pillars are the takbirs and standing.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the funeral prayer: ruling and pillars

cards.x: The deceased must be Muslim, washed, present and placed in front of the people, on the ground.

Four takbirs. After the first, praise Allah; after the second, send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ; after the third, make du'a for the deceased; after the fourth, give salam. The imam stands level with the chest.

checks.q: The funeral prayer is…
checks.why: If some pray it, the obligation is lifted from the rest.

checks.q: What is said after the third takbir?
checks.why: First praise, second blessings, third du'a, fourth salam.

checks.q: How many takbirs are in the funeral prayer?
checks.why: The prayer is four takbirs and standing.

checks.q: How many takbirs are in the funeral prayer?
checks.why: Four takbirs, standing, with no ruku' or sujud, ending with salam.

lessons.title: When someone dies
lessons.about: What to do from the last moments to the burial, and what follows.

cards.x: Turn the dying person towards the qiblah on the right side, and say the Shahadah gently near them so they may remember it, without pressing them to repeat it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what is done for one who is dying

cards.ar: الَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٞ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ ﴿١٥٦﴾
cards.x: …those who, when struck by a calamity, say: 'Truly we belong to Allah, and to Him we return.'
Close the eyes, tie the jaw, straighten the limbs and cover the body. Say: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' Hurry to wash, pray over and bury him, and settle his debts quickly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what is done when he dies

cards.x: Washing the deceased is fard kifayah. Men wash men and women wash women. A wife may wash her husband, but in the Hanafi school a husband does not wash his wife. Give him wudu first without rinsing the mouth and nose, then wash an odd number of times.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, preparing and washing him

cards.x: The sunnah shroud is white: three cloths for a man (a wrap, a long shirt and an outer sheet) and five for a woman (those three, a headscarf and a chest cloth).
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the shroud according to the Shari'ah

cards.x: After the funeral prayer, carry the bier quickly. Lay him in the grave on his right side facing the qiblah, saying 'Bismillahi wa 'ala millati Rasulillah.' Building over graves for show is disliked.

Weeping is allowed; wailing, tearing clothes and striking oneself are forbidden. Condolence is sunnah for three days. From his wealth come first the funeral costs, then his debts, then any bequest up to a third, then the shares of inheritance. A widow keeps an 'iddah of four months and ten days.

checks.q: How is the deceased laid in the grave?
checks.a: On the right side, facing the qiblah
w: On the back, feet to the qiblah
checks.why: Facing the qiblah on the right side, saying 'Bismillahi wa 'ala millati Rasulillah'.

checks.q: How many cloths make the sunnah shroud for a man?
checks.why: Three for a man, five for a woman.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the shroud according to the Shari'ah

checks.q: From a deceased's wealth, what is paid after the funeral costs?
checks.why: Funeral costs, then debts, then a bequest up to a third, then inheritance.

checks.q: Crying at a death is…
checks.a: Allowed, but wailing and tearing clothes are forbidden
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ wept at the death of his son Ibrahim.

checks.q: What is the 'iddah of a widow who is not pregnant?
checks.why: Al-Baqarah 234 sets four months and ten days.

lessons.title: The two Eid prayers
lessons.about: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha: how the prayer is done.

cards.x: The Eid prayer is wajib on those for whom Jumu'ah is fard. It is two rak'ahs, prayed after sunrise until midday, with the khutbah after the prayer.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The two Eid prayers

cards.x: In the first rak'ah, after the opening praise, say three extra takbirs raising the hands, then recite. In the second, recite, then say three extra takbirs before going into ruku'.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The two Eid prayers

cards.x: Ghusl, wearing your best clothes, perfume, and saying the takbir. Eat something sweet, like dates, before Eid al-Fitr; on Eid al-Adha, delay eating until after the prayer.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The two Eid prayers

checks.q: What is the ruling of the Eid prayer in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Wajib on those for whom Jumu'ah is fard.

checks.q: How many extra takbirs are in each rak'ah of the Eid prayer?
checks.why: Three in the first before reciting, three in the second before ruku'.

checks.q: Is the Eid khutbah before or after the prayer?
checks.why: Unlike Jumu'ah, the Eid khutbah comes after the prayer.

checks.q: What is sunnah before going out on Eid al-Fitr?
checks.why: On Eid al-Adha, eating is delayed until after the prayer.

lessons.title: Ramadan: who fasts and how it begins
lessons.about: Conditions, the intention and sighting the moon.

cards.x: Fasting Ramadan is fard on every Muslim who is sane and has reached puberty.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ﴿١٨٣﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may become mindful of Allah.

cards.ar: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْءَانُ هُدٗى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٖ مِّنَ الْهُدَىٰ وَالْفُرْقَانِ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُواْ الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿١٨٥﴾
cards.x: The month of Ramadan, in which the Qur'an was sent down… whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it.
Its essence is holding back from eating, drinking and intercourse from true dawn to sunset, with the intention.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, its pillar; Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Fasting

cards.x: For a Ramadan fast, the intention is valid from the night until before the middle of the day (midway between dawn and sunset). But for a make-up (qada') fast or an expiation fast, the intention must be made before dawn.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, fasts that need no fixed intention

cards.x: Ramadan begins by sighting its crescent, or by completing thirty days of Sha'ban if the sky is cloudy.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how Ramadan is established

checks.q: Until when can you make the intention for a Ramadan fast?
checks.a: Before the middle of the day
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: from the night until before the 'great forenoon', the middle of the day.

checks.q: If the moon cannot be seen on the 29th of Sha'ban…
checks.why: Ramadan is established by sighting or by completing thirty days.

checks.q: Fasting means holding back from…
checks.a: Eating, drinking and intercourse from dawn to sunset
w: Eating and drinking only, from dawn to sunset
Eating, drinking and talking, from dawn to dusk
Food only, from sunrise to sunset
checks.why: That is the pillar of the fast, with the intention.

checks.q: Until when can you make the intention for a Ramadan fast?
checks.a: Before the middle of the day
checks.why: The middle of the day here is halfway between true dawn and sunset, not the clock's midday.

checks.q: You are making up a missed Ramadan fast. When must you intend it?
checks.why: The midday allowance is for Ramadan itself. A make-up fast needs the intention before dawn.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, Ramadan: who fasts and how it begins

lessons.title: What does not break the fast
lessons.about: Forgetting, kohl, dust and other things that leave your fast intact.

cards.x: If you eat, drink or have intercourse having forgotten you are fasting, your fast is not broken.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

cards.x: Applying kohl or oil, smoke or dust entering the throat without your doing, and waking up in a state of janabah do not break the fast.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

cards.x: Backbiting does not break the fast, but it ruins its reward. Guard your tongue while fasting.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

cards.x: Forgetting is excused, but a mistake is not: if water slips down your throat while rinsing in wudu, the fast is broken and you make it up. Swallowing your own saliva, eye drops, a blood test and, according to most contemporary Hanafi scholars, an injection do not break it. An asthma inhaler, deliberately inhaling smoke and deliberately vomiting a mouthful do break it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Chapter on what breaks the fast

checks.q: You forgot you were fasting and drank water. Your fast…
w: Is broken and must be made up
checks.why: Eating or drinking having forgotten you are fasting does not break the fast.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

checks.q: Does applying kohl break the fast?
checks.why: Applying kohl does not break the fast.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

checks.q: Waking up in janabah while fasting…
w: Makes the fast disliked and void
checks.why: Waking up in a state of janabah does not break the fast. Make ghusl for the prayer.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

checks.q: You eat by mistake, forgetting you are fasting. What happens?
checks.a: The fast is not broken; carry on fasting
w: The fast is broken; make it up
Your fast is broken but no make-up is due
checks.why: Forgetting does not break the fast. Stop as soon as you remember.

checks.q: While rinsing your mouth in wudu, water slips down your throat. Your fast…
checks.a: Is broken; make up one day
w: Is fine, it was a mistake
Is fine if it was a little
checks.why: Forgetting is excused; a mistake is not. One make-up day, no expiation.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, What does not break the fast

lessons.title: Breaking the fast on purpose
lessons.about: When a make-up day is enough, and when the expiation is due.

cards.x: Deliberately eating, drinking, or having intercourse during a Ramadan fast, with no excuse and not forced, requires a make-up day and the expiation.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

cards.x: Fast two months in a row. If you truly cannot, feed sixty poor people two meals each, or give their value.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

cards.x: Some things break the fast but need only a make-up day, such as swallowing a pebble, or medicine reaching the stomach.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.q: Someone eats on purpose in Ramadan with no excuse. What is due?
checks.a: A make-up day and the expiation
checks.why: Deliberately eating in Ramadan with no excuse requires both a make-up day and the expiation.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.q: The expiation for breaking a Ramadan fast, for one who can fast, is…
checks.a: Fasting two months in a row
checks.why: The expiation is fasting two months in a row. Feeding sixty poor people is only for one who truly cannot fast.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.q: Swallowing a small pebble while fasting requires…
checks.why: Swallowing a pebble breaks the fast but needs only a make-up day, not the expiation.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.a: Fasting two months in a row

lessons.title: Who may leave the fast
lessons.about: Travellers, the ill, menstruation and the very old.

cards.x: A traveller and someone who is ill may break the fast and make it up later.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

cards.x: A woman in menstruation or post-natal bleeding does not fast, and makes up the days later. She does not make up the prayers.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

cards.x: Someone too old to fast who will not become able gives a fidyah for each day instead.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

cards.x: A pregnant or nursing woman who fears harm to herself or her child may leave the fast and makes it up later, with no fidyah. A traveller may break the fast, but fasting is better if it is not a hardship.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may leave the fast

checks.q: A woman misses fasts because of menstruation. She…
checks.why: She makes up the fasts later. She does not make up the prayers.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

checks.q: Who may break the fast and make it up later?
checks.why: A traveller may break the fast and make it up later, as may someone who is ill.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

checks.q: A very old person who cannot fast…
checks.a: Gives a fidyah for each day
checks.why: Someone too old to fast, who will not become able, gives a fidyah for each day.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

checks.q: A nursing mother fears fasting will harm her baby. What applies?
checks.a: She may leave it and make up the days later
w: She pays fidyah and never makes up
checks.why: She makes up the days later, with no fidyah.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may leave the fast

lessons.title: Who pays zakat
lessons.about: Who owes zakat, the nisab, and what happens with debts.

cards.x: Zakat is fard on a free, adult, sane Muslim who fully owns the nisab, once a full (lunar) year has passed on it.

cards.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ الصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ الزَّكَوٰةَ وَارْكَعُواْ مَعَ الرَّـٰكِعِينَ ﴿٤٣﴾
cards.x: Establish the prayer, give the zakat, and bow with those who bow.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ كَثِيرٗا مِّنَ الْأَحْبَارِ وَالرُّهْبَانِ لَيَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَٰلَ النَّاسِ بِالْبَٰطِلِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٖ ﴿٣٤﴾
cards.x: …those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah: give them tidings of a painful punishment.
The nisab is the minimum wealth on which zakat is due: 200 dirhams of silver (about 612 g) or 20 mithqals of gold (about 87.5 g), or the same value in money or trade goods.
Take away what you owe. If what remains still reaches the nisab, zakat is due on it.

Count cash, savings, gold and silver (including jewellery worn every day, in the Hanafi school) and goods bought to sell. Your home, car, furniture and clothes for use are not counted. Gold, silver and cash are added together. For money, many Hanafi scholars today use the silver nisab, as it is better for the poor.

checks.q: When does zakat become due on your wealth?
checks.a: A lunar year after owning the nisab
w: As soon as you own the nisab
At the start of every Ramadan
Once a month on what you earn
checks.why: The nisab is the minimum amount. Zakat is due after a lunar year with it.

checks.q: The nisab is the minimum wealth for zakat. What is the nisab of gold?
checks.why: Gold: 20 mithqals (about 87.5 g). Silver: 200 dirhams (about 612 g).

checks.q: A person has the nisab but also owes debts. What happens?
checks.a: Debts come off first; zakat is due if the rest reaches the nisab
w: Debts are ignored; zakat is due on everything
Zakat is paid first; debts are paid from the rest
No zakat is due at all while any debt remains
checks.why: Subtract what you owe; if what remains still reaches the nisab, zakat is due.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, is zakat due on gold jewellery a woman wears?
checks.a: Yes, it is counted with her wealth
checks.why: In the Hanafi school gold and silver are counted whether worn or stored.

checks.q: Which of these is counted for zakat?
checks.why: Cash, savings, gold, silver and trade goods are counted; things for personal use are not.

lessons.title: How much, and on what
lessons.about: The rate, trade goods, and giving zakat discreetly.

w: Only if you sell them that year

lessons.title: Who may receive zakat
lessons.about: Who zakat may be given to, and who it may not.

cards.x: The poor, the needy, those who collect it, those in debt, those striving in the path of Allah, the stranded traveller, and (in its time) freeing captives.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, who may receive zakat

cards.ar: إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَٰتُ لِلْفُقَرَآءِ وَالْمَسَٰكِينِ وَالْعَٰمِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَفِي الرِّقَابِ وَالْغَٰرِمِينَ وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ فَرِيضَةٗ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٞ ﴿٦٠﴾
cards.x: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy, those who work to collect it, those whose hearts are to be won over, freeing captives, those in debt, the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveller: an obligation from Allah. Allah is Knowing, Wise.
You may not give your zakat to your parents, grandparents, children or grandchildren, nor to your spouse (a wife giving to her husband is also not allowed, in Imam Abu Hanifah's view).

cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may receive zakat

checks.q: How are poor descendants of Banu Hashim helped?

checks.q: Which may receive zakat?
checks.why: The stranded traveller is one of those who may receive zakat.

checks.q: May you give your zakat to your own mother?
checks.a: No, not to parents, children or spouse

checks.a: No, it must be given to a poor person to own
w: Yes, it is the best use

checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may receive zakat

lessons.title: Zakat al-Fitr
lessons.about: Who pays it, how much and when.

cards.x: It is wajib on a free Muslim who owns the nisab beyond his home, clothes, furniture and basic needs. He pays for himself and his young children.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Sadaqat al-Fitr

cards.x: Half a sa' of wheat or wheat flour (about 1.6–2 kg), or a full sa' of dates, raisins or barley (about 3.2–4 kg), or the value of it in money, which is what most people give today. A sa' is a measure of volume from the time of the Prophet ﷺ, so the weight in kg is an estimate.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Sadaqat al-Fitr

cards.x: It becomes due at dawn on the day of Eid. It is recommended to give it before going out to the Eid prayer; giving it earlier is allowed, and delaying it does not cancel it.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Sadaqat al-Fitr

checks.q: When does zakat al-fitr become due?
checks.a: At dawn on the day of Eid
checks.why: Al-Quduri: it is tied to the dawn of the day of Fitr.

checks.q: Who does a father pay it for?
w: His wife and adult children only
checks.why: He pays for himself and his young children; not for his wife or adult children.

checks.q: If it is delayed past Eid…
checks.why: Delaying it does not make it fall away.

checks.q: About how much wheat is half a sa' for zakat al-Fitr?
checks.why: Half a sa' of wheat is roughly 1.6–2 kg; most people give its value in money.

lessons.title: Qurbani (udhiyah)
lessons.about: The sacrifice of Eid al-Adha: who must give it, and how.

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, the qurbani is wajib on a free, resident Muslim who owns the nisab beyond their basic needs on the days of sacrifice. It is for oneself, not for one's children.
From after the Eid prayer on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah until sunset on the 12th. Where there is no Eid prayer, from dawn on the 10th.
A sheep or goat of at least one year counts for one person. A cow (two years) or a camel (five years) counts for up to seven people, each with a full share. It must be free of major defects.
It is recommended to divide it into thirds: for your family, for relatives and friends, and for the poor. The skin may be given away but not sold.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, what is the ruling of qurbani for someone who owns the nisab?
checks.why: Wajib on the free, resident Muslim who owns the nisab on the days of sacrifice.

checks.q: How many people can share one cow for qurbani?
checks.why: A cow or camel counts for up to seven; a sheep or goat for one.

checks.q: When may the qurbani be slaughtered?
checks.a: After the Eid prayer on the 10th until sunset on the 12th
checks.why: Slaughtering before the Eid prayer, where it is held, does not count.

checks.q: How old must a goat be for qurbani?
checks.why: A sheep of six months that looks like a yearling is also accepted.

lessons.title: Who must perform Hajj
lessons.about: The conditions, and the months of Hajj.

cards.x: Hajj is fard on free, adult, sane and healthy Muslims who can afford the provision and transport, beyond their home, their needs and their family's maintenance until they return, when the road is safe.

cards.ar: فِيهِ ءَايَٰتُ بَيِّنَٰتٞ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ ءَامِنٗا وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلٗا وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَٰلَمِينَ ﴿٩٧﴾
cards.x: Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to find a way there.
A woman must have a mahram or her husband with her if Makkah is three days' journey or more away. She may not go for Hajj without one of them.
The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

checks.q: Hajj is fard on someone who…
checks.a: Can afford travel beyond his needs and his family's upkeep
w: Has any savings at all, even if he is in debt
Can afford the travel, even if his family is left in need
Has already done 'umrah and lives near Makkah
checks.why: Al-Quduri ties it to affording provision and transport beyond needs and family maintenance, with a safe road.

checks.q: Can a woman go for Hajj without a mahram or husband, from far away?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: she may not perform Hajj without a mahram or husband if the journey is three days or more.

checks.q: Which are the months of Hajj?
checks.a: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
w: Only the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram
checks.why: Al-Quduri defines them in the chapter on tamattu'.

checks.q: May a woman travel for Hajj without a mahram or her husband?
checks.a: No, if Makkah is three days' journey or more
w: Yes, in a group of women
Yes, if she has the money
checks.why: Al-Quduri makes a mahram or husband a condition for her, from that distance.

lessons.title: The miqat and entering ihram
lessons.about: Where to enter ihram, and how.

cards.x: Do not pass these without ihram: Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah, Dhat 'Irq for Iraq, al-Juhfah for Syria, Qarn al-Manazil for Najd, and Yalamlam for Yemen. Entering ihram before them is allowed.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the miqats

cards.x: Make ghusl (or wudu, but ghusl is better), put on two clean sheets, a lower and an upper one, apply perfume if you have it, and pray two rak'ahs.

Say: 'O Allah, I intend Hajj, make it easy for me and accept it from me.' Then say the talbiyah: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayk la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika lak.' With the talbiyah you are in ihram.

checks.q: What is the miqat for people coming from Madinah?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah.

checks.q: When do you actually enter ihram?
checks.a: When you say the talbiyah with the intention
w: When you put on the two sheets
When you first see the Ka'bah
checks.why: 'When he says the talbiyah, he has entered ihram.'

checks.q: Before ihram, which is better?
checks.why: Ghusl or wudu, and ghusl is better.

checks.q: When do you actually enter ihram?
checks.a: With the intention and the talbiyah
w: When you put on the two sheets
When you first see the Ka'bah
checks.why: The sheets, ghusl and two rak'ahs prepare you; the intention with the talbiyah makes you muhrim.

lessons.title: What ihram forbids
lessons.about: What the muhrim must avoid.

cards.x: Avoid intimacy and its talk, sinning and arguing. Do not hunt, or point out or direct anyone to game.

cards.ar: الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٞ مَّعْلُومَٰتٞ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي الْحَجِّ وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٖ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوَىٰ وَاتَّقُونِ يَـٰٓأُوْلِي الْأَلْبَٰبِ ﴿١٩٧﴾
cards.x: Hajj is in well-known months. Whoever sets out to do Hajj in them, let there be no intimacy, no sinning and no quarrelling in Hajj.
A man does not wear a shirt, trousers, turban, cap, cloak or khuffs (unless he has no sandals, then he cuts them below the ankles), and does not cover his head or face.
Do not use perfume or anything scented, shave or remove any hair, trim the beard or cut the nails. Bathing, shade and wearing a money belt are allowed, with conditions: see the next point.

Bathing for cleanliness or to cool down is allowed, but: no scented soap, shower gel, shampoo or scented wipes, because the later Hanafi scholars count these as perfume, which brings a penalty. Al-Quduri says the muhrim does not wash his head or beard with khitmi (a cleansing plant). Use water, or unscented soap, and wash gently so that no hair falls out. Do not dry yourself with a scented towel.

A woman is like a man in all this, except that she covers her head and keeps cloth from touching her face (if needed she lets something hang in front that does not touch it), does not raise her voice in the talbiyah, does not jog in tawaf or run between the green markers, and trims her hair instead of shaving.

checks.q: May a man in ihram cover his head?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: he does not cover his head or face.

checks.q: Which is allowed in ihram?
checks.a: Bathing with water or unscented soap
checks.why: Bathing is allowed, but scented soap, shower gel and shampoo count as perfume and bring a penalty. Wash gently so no hair falls.

checks.q: In ihram, a woman…
checks.a: Covers her head and uncovers her face
w: Uncovers her head and covers her face
Covers both her head and face
Shaves her head at the end
checks.why: She keeps her head covered and her face uncovered.

checks.q: In ihram you want a shower. Which is right?
checks.a: Use water or unscented soap, and wash gently
w: Any shower gel is fine as it is only for washing
Use scented shampoo but not perfume
Showering is not allowed in ihram
checks.why: Scented soap and shampoo count as perfume. Bathing itself is allowed, without making hair fall.

lessons.title: The three ways of Hajj
lessons.about: Ifrad, tamattu' and qiran.

cards.x: Entering ihram for Hajj alone.

Entering ihram for 'umrah in the months of Hajj, completing it and leaving ihram, then entering ihram for Hajj from Makkah on the 8th (Yawm al-Tarwiyah). A sacrifice is due; if you cannot, fast three days during Hajj and seven when you return.
Entering ihram for 'umrah and Hajj together from the miqat. In the Hanafi school qiran is the best, then tamattu', then ifrad. It too requires a sacrifice.
The people of Makkah do not do tamattu' or qiran; only ifrad.

checks.q: Which way of Hajj is best in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: qiran is better than tamattu' and ifrad.

checks.q: In tamattu', when do you enter ihram for Hajj?
checks.a: On the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, from Makkah
w: On the 10th, after the Eid prayer
checks.why: After completing the 'umrah you stay in Makkah and enter ihram for Hajj on Yawm al-Tarwiyah.

checks.q: A mutamatti' who cannot afford the sacrifice…
checks.a: Fasts three days in Hajj and seven at home
w: Fasts ten days, all in Makkah
checks.why: Three days during Hajj and seven when he returns.

lessons.title: 'Umrah
lessons.about: Its ruling and its acts.

cards.x: 'Umrah is a sunnah. It can be done at any time of year, but is disliked on five days: the day of 'Arafah, the day of sacrifice and the three days of tashriq.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on missing Hajj

cards.x: 'Umrah is: ihram, tawaf, sa'y, and shaving or trimming.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on missing Hajj

cards.x: The one in 'umrah stops the talbiyah when he starts the tawaf.

checks.q: What is the ruling of 'umrah in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'umrah is sunnah.

checks.q: On which day is 'umrah disliked?
checks.why: It is disliked on 'Arafah, the day of sacrifice and the days of tashriq.

checks.q: What are the acts of 'umrah?
checks.a: Ihram, tawaf, sa'y, then shaving or trimming
checks.why: Al-Quduri lists exactly these.

lessons.title: Tawaf and sa'y
lessons.about: Arriving in Makkah.

cards.x: Enter al-Masjid al-Haram. On seeing the House say takbir and tahlil. Begin at the Black Stone: face it, say takbir, raise your hands and touch and kiss it if you can without harming anyone.

Go round the House seven times, with the Ka'bah on your left, outside the Hatim. Men uncover the right shoulder (idtiba') and jog (raml) in the first three circuits, then walk. Touch the Stone each time you pass it if you can, and end with it.
Pray two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim, or wherever is easy in the masjid.

Go to al-Safa, face the House, say takbir and tahlil, send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ and make du'a. Walk to al-Marwah, men running between the two green markers. That is one circuit; complete seven, starting at al-Safa and ending at al-Marwah.

checks.q: Where does each circuit of tawaf begin?
w: At the door of the Ka'bah
checks.why: Al-Quduri: begin at the Black Stone.

checks.q: In which circuits do men jog (raml)?
checks.why: Raml is in the first three circuits.

checks.q: Sa'y starts at… and ends at…
checks.why: Seven circuits, starting at al-Safa and ending at al-Marwah.

lessons.title: Mina, 'Arafah and Muzdalifah
lessons.about: The 8th and 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

cards.x: On the 8th (Yawm al-Tarwiyah), after Fajr in Makkah, go to Mina and stay until you pray Fajr on the day of 'Arafah.

cards.ar: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُواْ فَضْلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَإِذَآ أَفَضْتُم مِّنْ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَاذْكُرُواْ اللَّهَ عِندَ الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ وَاذْكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الضَّآلِّينَ ﴿١٩٨﴾
cards.x: When you pour down from 'Arafat, remember Allah at the Sacred Landmark (Muzdalifah).

The standing at 'Arafah is the heart of Hajj. Whoever is at 'Arafah at any time from midday on the 9th until dawn on the 10th has caught the Hajj. All of 'Arafah is a place of standing except Batn 'Uranah. Strive in du'a.
After sunset, leave calmly for Muzdalifah. Pray Maghrib and 'Isha' there together. After Fajr, stand and make du'a, then leave for Mina before sunrise.

checks.q: When is the time for standing at 'Arafah?
checks.a: From midday on the 9th until dawn on the 10th
w: From sunset on the 9th until midnight
checks.why: Al-Quduri: from the sun's decline on the day of 'Arafah to dawn on the day of sacrifice.

checks.q: Where are Maghrib and 'Isha' prayed on the night of the 9th?
checks.why: Praying Maghrib on the road is not valid in the view of Abu Hanifah and Muhammad.

checks.q: Which part of 'Arafah is not a place of standing?
checks.why: All of 'Arafah is valid except Batn 'Uranah.

checks.q: What is the heart of Hajj, without which it is missed?
checks.why: 'Hajj is 'Arafah.' Whoever is there between midday on the 9th and dawn on the 10th has caught it.

lessons.title: The Day of Sacrifice and after
lessons.about: Stoning, sacrifice, shaving and tawaf al-ziyarah.

cards.x: On the 10th, stone Jamrat al-'Aqabah with seven pebbles, saying takbir with each. Stop the talbiyah with the first pebble.
Then sacrifice, then shave or trim; shaving is better. Now everything is lawful except intimacy.

Go to Makkah on the 10th, 11th or 12th and perform tawaf al-ziyarah, seven circuits. This is the fard tawaf of Hajj. After it, intimacy becomes lawful. Delaying it past these days requires a sacrifice, according to Abu Hanifah.

Return to Mina. On the 11th and 12th, after midday, stone the three jamarat, starting with the one nearest the Masjid al-Khayf, seven pebbles each, stopping to make du'a after the first two. You may leave on the 12th or stay for the 13th.

checks.q: Which jamrah is stoned on the 10th?
checks.why: On the day of sacrifice only Jamrat al-'Aqabah is stoned.

checks.q: What is the fard tawaf of Hajj?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'This tawaf is the one that is fard in Hajj.'

checks.q: After stoning, sacrificing and shaving, what remains forbidden until tawaf al-ziyarah?
checks.why: Everything becomes lawful except intimacy, which becomes lawful after tawaf al-ziyarah.

lessons.title: Farewell, and the wajibs of Hajj
lessons.about: Tawaf al-Wada', and what a sacrifice repairs.

cards.x: Before leaving Makkah, perform tawaf al-sadr (the farewell tawaf), seven circuits without jogging. It is wajib, except for the people of Makkah. A woman who gets her period after tawaf al-ziyarah may leave without it.
Leaving sa'y, the standing at Muzdalifah, the stoning, or the farewell tawaf requires a sheep, and the Hajj is still complete.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the violations of the muhrim

cards.x: Missing the standing at 'Arafah means the Hajj is missed. Tawaf al-ziyarah must be done; a sacrifice cannot replace it.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the violations of the muhrim

checks.q: Someone left out sa'y. What follows?
checks.a: A sheep is due; the Hajj is complete
w: The Hajj is invalid and must be repeated
Nothing is due; the Hajj is complete
He fasts three days; the Hajj is complete
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'Whoever leaves the sa'y owes a sheep, and his Hajj is complete.'

checks.q: Is the farewell tawaf wajib on the people of Makkah?
checks.why: It is wajib except on the people of Makkah.

checks.q: A woman's period starts after tawaf al-ziyarah. Before leaving she…
checks.a: May leave without the farewell tawaf
w: Must wait until she is pure
checks.why: Al-Quduri: she leaves, and owes nothing for missing tawaf al-sadr.

title: Halal & Haram
sub: Food, dress, the gaze and earning, and the levels of carefulness

lessons.title: Why halal matters
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali on the lawful and the unlawful.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is good and accepts only what is good. He mentioned a traveller, dishevelled and dusty, raising his hands: 'O Lord!', while his food, drink and clothing are haram. 'How can he be answered?'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim; quoted in Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُواْ مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَٰلٗا طَيِّبٗا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٰتِ الشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوّٞ مُّبِينٌ ﴿١٦٨﴾
cards.x: O people, eat of what is on the earth, lawful and good, and do not follow the footsteps of Shaytan.
Imam al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ opens this book with the virtue of the lawful and the blame of the unlawful, bringing verses and hadiths on how what we consume affects our worship.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Lawful and Unlawful

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: the halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. Whoever avoids the doubtful has protected his religion and honour.

checks.q: Why was the traveller's du'a not answered?
checks.a: His food, drink and clothing were haram
w: He did not raise his hands high enough
He was travelling and in a hurry
checks.why: In the hadith, the reason given is that his food, drink and clothing were haram.

checks.q: Between clear halal and clear haram are…
checks.why: Between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know.

checks.q: Avoiding doubtful things protects…
checks.why: 'Whoever avoids the doubtful has protected his religion and his honour.'

lessons.title: The major sins
lessons.about: What every Muslim must avoid.

cards.x: Major sins (kaba'ir) are those Allah threatened with the Fire, curse or a set punishment. Avoiding them is fard; Allah promises to forgive the minor sins of those who avoid the major ones.

cards.ar: إِن تَجْتَنِبُواْ كَبَآئِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَنُدْخِلْكُم مُّدْخَلٗا كَرِيمٗا ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your lesser sins and admit you through a noble entrance.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اجْتَنِبُواْ كَثِيرٗا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٞ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُواْ وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتٗا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ وَاتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿١٢﴾
cards.x: Do not spy, and do not backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it.

Shirk, killing unjustly, magic, leaving the prayer, withholding zakat, disobeying parents, zina, drinking alcohol, riba, consuming an orphan's wealth, false witness, slandering chaste people, and fleeing the battlefield.
Backbiting (saying what a person would dislike, even if true), carrying tales, and lying are major sins too. They are easy on the tongue and heavy on the Scale.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Banes of the Tongue

checks.q: What does Allah promise those who avoid the major sins?
w: That they will never be tested
checks.why: 'If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your lesser sins.' (al-Nisa' 31)

checks.q: Saying something true about a person that they would dislike is…
checks.why: If it is true it is backbiting; if false it is slander, which is worse.

checks.q: Which of these is a major sin?
w: Eating with the left hand by mistake
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ counted disobeying parents among the greatest sins.

checks.q: Leaving the prayer out of laziness is…
checks.why: It is among the gravest sins; make it up and repent.

lessons.title: Rights of parents and family
lessons.about: Kindness to parents and keeping ties of kinship.

cards.x: Allah joined thanks to Him with thanks to parents. Obey them in everything that is not sin, speak to them gently, never say even 'uff', serve them, and pray for them, in life and after death.

cards.ar: وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفّٖ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلٗا كَرِيمٗا ﴿٢٣﴾
cards.x: Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and be good to parents. If one or both reach old age with you, do not say to them even 'uff', nor scold them, but speak to them with noble words.
A man asked who most deserves his good company. The Prophet ﷺ said: your mother, your mother, your mother, then your father.
Keeping ties with relatives (silat al-rahim) is wajib, and cutting them is a major sin. Visit, help and keep in touch with them, even if they do not do the same.

checks.q: Your parents tell you to do something sinful. What do you do?
checks.a: Refuse gently, and keep being kind to them
checks.why: No obedience to anyone in disobeying Allah, but you stay kind and respectful.

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ name three times as most deserving of good company?
checks.why: Your mother, your mother, your mother, then your father.

checks.q: What is the ruling of keeping ties with relatives?
checks.a: Wajib, and cutting them is a major sin
w: Only with those who are kind to you
checks.why: Keep ties even with those who cut you off.

lessons.title: Marriage and the family
lessons.about: What every Muslim must know before marrying and while raising a family.

cards.x: Marriage (nikah) is made by an offer and an acceptance spoken in the presence of two Muslim witnesses: two men, or one man and two women.

cards.ar: وَمِنْ ءَايَٰتِهِٓ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجٗا لِّتَسْكُنُوٓاْ إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةٗ وَرَحْمَةً إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتٖ لِّقَوْمٖ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ ﴿٢١﴾
cards.x: Among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves so that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy.
The mahr is the wife's right, owed by the husband, whether or not it was named. In the Hanafi school it is at least ten dirhams of silver.

No one may marry a woman without her consent. In the Hanafi school an adult woman's marriage is valid without her guardian, but it is sunnah for him to arrange it, and he may object if the husband is not a suitable match.

The husband must provide his wife's food, clothing and housing, and live with her in kindness. The wife obeys him in what is right and guards his home and honour. The Prophet ﷺ said: the best of you are the best to their wives.

Divorce (talaq) is the most disliked of lawful things to Allah. The sunnah way is one talaq in a time of purity without intimacy. Three talaqs said at once count as three in the Hanafi school, and saying them is sinful. A divorced woman who menstruates keeps an 'iddah of three periods.
Give children good names, teach them the prayer at seven, and be fair between them. The Prophet ﷺ said Jibril kept advising him about the neighbour until he thought he would make him an heir.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

checks.q: What makes a nikah valid?
checks.a: Offer and acceptance before two witnesses
w: A signature at the registry only
checks.why: Al-Quduri: offer and acceptance, with two witnesses.

checks.q: Whose right is the mahr?
checks.why: It is owed to her by her husband.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, three talaqs said at once count as…
checks.a: Three, and saying them that way is sinful
checks.why: They take effect as three, so the marriage cannot be resumed without the conditions the Qur'an sets.

checks.q: May a woman be married without her consent?
checks.why: Her consent is required.

checks.q: At what age are children taught to pray?
checks.why: Teach them at seven; be firmer at ten (Abu Dawud).
checks.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

lessons.title: The four degrees of carefulness
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's levels of wara'.

cards.x: The first degree, of the upright, is avoiding what the fatwa says is haram. The second, of the righteous, is also avoiding what is doubtful.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

cards.x: The third, of the God-fearing, is leaving some things that are fine for fear they lead to what is not.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

cards.x: The fourth, of the siddiqin, is leaving even what is harmless if it is taken for other than Allah, or not to gain strength for His worship.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

checks.q: Avoiding what the fatwa calls haram is the wara' of…
checks.why: The first degree, required of everyone, is the wara' of the upright.

checks.q: Leaving harmless things done for other than Allah is the wara' of…
checks.why: Al-Ghazali calls this highest degree the wara' of the siddiqin.

checks.q: How many degrees of wara' does al-Ghazali give?
checks.why: He describes four: of the upright, the righteous, the God-fearing and the siddiqin.

lessons.title: Food and slaughter
lessons.about: What may be eaten, and whose slaughter is lawful.

cards.x: The slaughter of a Muslim or of a Jew or Christian (Ahl al-Kitab) is halal, but only if it is a real slaughter: the throat and main vessels cut while the animal is alive, and no name other than Allah's invoked. Meat killed by stunning, a machine or any other way is not halal, whoever did it. The slaughter of a Magian, an apostate or an idol-worshipper is not eaten.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.ar: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ الْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَالنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بِالْأَزْلَٰمِ ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَٰمَ دِينٗا فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٖ لِّإِثْمٖ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and what was dedicated to other than Allah…

cards.ar: وَلَا تَأْكُلُواْ مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٞ وَإِنَّ الشَّيَٰطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِهِمْ لِيُجَٰدِلُوكُمْ وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ ﴿١٢١﴾
cards.x: And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.
If the one slaughtering leaves out Allah's name on purpose, the animal is carrion and may not be eaten. If he forgot, it may be eaten.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.x: Of sea creatures, only fish are eaten in the Hanafi school, and a fish that died by itself and floats is disliked. Locusts may be eaten without slaughter.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.x: Pork and everything from it, carrion (an animal not properly slaughtered), flowing blood, alcohol and anything that intoxicates, predators with fangs, birds with talons, and donkeys. Today, check ingredients such as gelatine, animal fat and alcohol in flavourings.

checks.q: Is meat slaughtered by a Christian halal?
checks.a: Yes, if he slaughters properly and names no one but Allah
w: Yes, however the animal was killed
checks.why: Al-Quduri: the slaughter of a Muslim or a Kitabi is halal. It must be a real slaughter; stunned-to-death or machine-killed meat is not halal from anyone.

checks.q: The slaughterer forgot to say bismillah. The meat…
checks.why: Leaving it out by forgetting does not make it haram; leaving it on purpose does.

checks.q: Which sea creatures may be eaten in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: of water animals, only fish are eaten.

checks.q: Gelatine in sweets usually comes from…
checks.a: Pork or unslaughtered animals, so check before eating
checks.why: Gelatine is commonly made from pork or non-halal animals. Look for halal or plant-based versions.

lessons.title: Gold, silk and vessels
lessons.about: What men and women may wear and use.

cards.x: Silk is not lawful for men to wear, except a trim or border up to four fingers wide. It is lawful for women.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: Men may not wear gold or silver, except a silver ring (less than one mithqal, about 4.3 g), a belt fitting and a sword decoration of silver. Women may wear gold and silver.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: Eating, drinking, oiling and perfuming from vessels of gold and silver is not allowed, for men or women. Glass and crystal are fine.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

checks.q: May a man wear a gold ring?
w: Yes, if it is a wedding ring
checks.why: Men may not wear gold. A silver ring of less than one mithqal (about 4.3 g) is allowed.

checks.q: Drinking from a silver cup is…
checks.a: Not allowed for men or women
checks.why: Eating and drinking from gold and silver vessels is not allowed for either.

checks.q: Wearing silk is lawful for…
checks.why: Silk is not lawful for men to wear, and lawful for women.

lessons.title: Lowering the gaze
lessons.about: What may be looked at, according to al-Quduri.

cards.x: A man may not look at a woman who is not his mahram except at her face and hands. If he is not safe from desire, he does not look even at her face, except for a need.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.ar: قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمْ ذَٰلِكَ أَزْكَىٰ لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرُ بِمَا يَصْنَعُونَ ﴿٣٠﴾ وَقُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحْفَظْنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوْ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ التَّـٰبِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُوْلِي الْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ أَوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَٰتِ النِّسَآءِ وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity… and tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity.
A judge, a witness and a doctor may look as their work requires.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: A man may look at another man except between the navel and the knee.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

checks.q: If a man fears desire, may he look at a non-mahram's face?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: if he is not safe from desire he does not look even at her face, except for a need.

checks.q: Which part of a man may another man not look at?
checks.a: Between the navel and the knee
w: Only between the navel and the chest
checks.why: Between the navel and the knee is 'awrah for men.

checks.q: Who may look as their work requires?
checks.why: A judge, a witness and a doctor may look as needed.

lessons.title: Riba (interest)
lessons.about: What riba is, and why it is so serious.

cards.x: Riba is haram. The Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who pays it, the one who writes it and its two witnesses, and said: they are all the same.

cards.ar: الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَوٰاْ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطَٰنُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبَوٰاْ وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَوٰاْ فَمَن جَآءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِ فَانتَهَىٰ فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ وَأَمْرُهُٓ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ ﴿٢٧٥﴾
cards.x: Those who consume riba will not stand except as one stands whom Shaytan has struck with madness. That is because they say trade is just like riba, but Allah has made trade lawful and riba unlawful.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ وَذَرُواْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَوٰٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴿٢٧٨﴾ فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٖ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَٰلِكُمْ لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ ﴿٢٧٩﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and give up what remains of riba, if you are believers. If you do not, then be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger.
Al-Quduri: riba is in anything measured by volume or weight, when sold for the same kind with an increase. Like for like is allowed; with an increase it is not.
Al-Ghazali lists riba among the common wrongs of the marketplace that must be stopped.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ curse in the hadith on riba?
checks.a: The one who takes it, pays it, writes it and witnesses it
w: Only the one who takes it
The one who takes it and the one who pays it
checks.why: All four were cursed, and he said they are all the same.

checks.q: Selling a kilo of dates for two kilos of dates, on the spot, is…
checks.why: Same kind, weighed or measured, with an increase is riba.

checks.q: Selling gold for the same weight of gold, hand to hand, is…
checks.why: Like for like of the same kind is allowed.

lessons.title: Money: riba, loans and earning
lessons.about: How to keep your income and spending halal in a world built on interest.

cards.x: Riba (interest) is among the major sins. Allah made trade lawful and riba unlawful, and told those who will not give it up to expect war from Allah and His Messenger.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَٰمُ رِجْسٞ مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَٰنِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٩٠﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, wine, gambling, idols and divining arrows are only filth from the work of Shaytan, so avoid it, that you may succeed.

cards.ar: الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَوٰاْ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطَٰنُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبَوٰاْ وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَوٰاْ فَمَن جَآءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِ فَانتَهَىٰ فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ وَأَمْرُهُٓ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ ﴿٢٧٥﴾
cards.x: Allah has made trade lawful and riba unlawful.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ وَذَرُواْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَوٰٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴿٢٧٨﴾ فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٖ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَٰلِكُمْ لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ ﴿٢٧٩﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and give up what remains of riba, if you are believers. If you do not, then be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger.

Any loan where you must pay back more than you borrowed is riba: a mortgage with interest, a personal loan, car finance with interest, an overdraft or a credit card that charges interest. There is no exception for buying a home, however normal it has become.

The Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who takes riba, the one who pays it, the one who writes it and its two witnesses, and said they are all the same. So a job that arranges or writes interest contracts is not halal income.
Do not take interest on savings. If a bank has paid interest into your account, do not use it for yourself: give it away to the poor without intending reward, to rid yourself of it.
Gambling is haram in every form: betting, lottery tickets, scratchcards, and paid entries where you may win more than you paid or lose it.
Earning a halal living is an obligation. Before taking out insurance, a pension, investments or any finance product, ask a qualified scholar: many contain riba or gambling hidden in the terms.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Earning and Livelihood

checks.q: Is a mortgage with interest allowed to buy a family home?
checks.a: No; any loan with interest is riba
w: Yes, a home is a necessity
Yes, if the rate is low
Yes, for a first home only
checks.why: Riba is haram whatever it is used for.

checks.q: A bank has paid interest into your savings. What do you do?
checks.a: Give it to the poor without intending reward
checks.why: It is not yours to use; you rid yourself of it.

checks.q: Buying a lottery ticket is…
w: Allowed if it is for charity
checks.why: Gambling is filth from the work of Shaytan (al-Ma'idah 90).

checks.q: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ curse in the hadith of riba?
checks.a: The taker, the payer, the writer and the witnesses
checks.why: He said they are all the same.

lessons.title: Honesty in trade
lessons.about: Cheating in the market, from al-Ghazali.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali names, among the common wrongs of the market, lying about what you paid for goods so you can sell at a 'profit'. Whoever knows of it should tell the buyer.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good: wrongs of the market

cards.ar: وَيْلٞ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ ﴿١﴾ الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتَالُواْ عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ ﴿٢﴾ وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَو وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: Woe to those who give short measure: who, when they take from people, take in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, give them less.
Hiding a fault in what you sell is also forbidden. Whoever knows the fault must point it out, or he is content with his brother's loss.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good: wrongs of the market

cards.x: Giving short weight or short measure must be stopped. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever cheats us is not one of us.'
cards.src: Ihya', wrongs of the market; Hadith, Sahih Muslim

checks.q: Saying 'I bought it for ten' when you paid less is…
checks.why: Al-Ghazali lists lying in the cost price among the wrongs of the market.

checks.q: If you know a fault in an item you are selling…
checks.why: Hiding it means being content with your brother's loss.

checks.q: 'Whoever cheats us…'
checks.why: The hadith in Sahih Muslim.

title: Dealing with Doubts
sub: What to do with doubts, from the Prophet ﷺ and Imam al-Ghazali

lessons.title: A doubt is not disbelief
lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said to Companions troubled by thoughts.

cards.x: Some Companions told the Prophet ﷺ they found thoughts in themselves too terrible to speak. He asked, 'Do you really find that?' They said yes. He said: 'That is clear faith.'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan comes and asks: who created this, who created that, until he asks who created your Lord. When that happens, seek refuge in Allah and stop.
Being troubled by such a thought shows your faith rejects it. You are not blamed for a passing thought.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ call hating these whispers?

checks.q: When the thought 'who created Allah?' comes, you should…
checks.a: Seek refuge in Allah and stop
checks.why: The hadith's instruction is to seek refuge in Allah and stop.

checks.q: Is a person sinful for a passing doubt they dislike?
w: Only if it lasts a day
checks.why: Disliking it shows faith; a passing thought is not held against you.

lessons.title: Al-Ghazali's own doubts
lessons.about: A great Imam's honest account of his crisis.

cards.x: Imam al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ wrote that doubt overcame him so strongly that for nearly two months he could not trust even the basic truths of the mind.
He was cured, he says, not by arranging proofs, but by a light that Allah cast into his breast. That light is the key to most knowledge.
Al-Ghazali warns that whoever thinks unveiling depends only on written proofs has narrowed the vast mercy of Allah.

checks.q: How long did al-Ghazali's worst doubt last?
checks.why: He says it lasted close to two months.

checks.q: What cured al-Ghazali, in his words?
checks.a: A light Allah cast into his breast
w: A debate he won against a philosopher
A book of philosophy he read
checks.why: Not arranged proofs but a light Allah cast into his breast.

checks.q: What does al-Ghazali say about Allah's mercy?
checks.a: It is wider than written proofs alone
checks.why: Thinking unveiling depends only on proofs narrows Allah's vast mercy.

lessons.title: Know the truth, then its people
lessons.about: Judging ideas by truth, not by who says them.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali quotes 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: 'Do not know the truth by men. Know the truth, and you will know its people.'
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

cards.x: He says it is the habit of weak minds to know truth by people, instead of knowing people by the truth.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

cards.x: Al-Ghazali examined the theologians, the philosophers, the Batinis and the Sufis, and found what he sought in the way of the Sufis: knowledge joined with action.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the ways of the Sufis

checks.q: Who said 'Know the truth and you will know its people'?
checks.a: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
checks.why: Al-Ghazali quotes it from 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

checks.q: Al-Ghazali calls knowing truth by people…
checks.why: He says the intelligent person knows people by the truth, not the other way round.

checks.q: Where did al-Ghazali find what he was seeking?
checks.why: He found it in the way of the Sufis, which joins knowledge and action.

lessons.title: How we know the Prophet ﷺ is true
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's way to certainty about prophethood.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali says: if you know some medicine, you can recognise a real doctor by his words and his work. In the same way you can come to know the Prophet ﷺ by his words and states.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the reality of prophethood

cards.x: Then strengthen it by experience: act on what he ﷺ taught about worship, and see how it purifies the heart.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the reality of prophethood

cards.x: Al-Ghazali cites: 'Whoever acts on what he knows, Allah gives him knowledge of what he did not know.' You will find it true.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the reality of prophethood

checks.q: Al-Ghazali compares knowing the Prophet ﷺ to knowing…
checks.a: A real doctor by his words and work
w: A king by his crown and palace
A rich man by his house and clothes
A stranger by his name and family
checks.why: As you can recognise a real doctor or faqih, you can recognise the Prophet ﷺ.

checks.q: How does al-Ghazali say certainty is strengthened?
checks.a: By acting on his teachings and seeing their effect on the heart
w: By reading the books of the philosophers closely
By waiting to see a miracle with his own eyes
By arguing with those who doubt until he wins
checks.why: Experience of his teachings purifying the heart strengthens certainty.

checks.q: Whoever acts on what he knows…
checks.a: Allah gives him knowledge of what he did not know
w: Has no more need of a teacher
Should stop learning and only act
checks.why: Al-Ghazali cites this saying as something you will find true by experience.

lessons.title: Leave what makes you doubt
lessons.about: Simple Prophetic advice for daily doubts.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.'
Allah says: 'Ask the people of remembrance if you do not know.' (al-Nahl 43) Doubts are answered by learning, not by hiding them.
Al-Ghazali describes leaving his position in Baghdad and turning to seclusion, disciplining the self and the remembrance of Allah.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the ways of the Sufis

checks.q: 'Leave what makes you doubt for…'
checks.a: What does not make you doubt
checks.why: The hadith: leave what makes you doubt for what does not.

checks.q: If you have a question about the religion, you should…
checks.why: 'Ask the people of remembrance if you do not know.' (al-Nahl 43)

checks.q: What did al-Ghazali turn to besides study?
checks.why: In al-Munqidh he describes leaving Baghdad for seclusion, discipline and dhikr.

lessons.title: Questions people ask today
lessons.about: Short, sound answers to the doubts you are most likely to meet.

cards.x: This world is a test, not the final home. Allah created death and life to test which of you is best in deeds. Every wrong will be settled on the Day of Judgement, and the patient will be given their reward without measure.

cards.ar: الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلٗا وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفُورُ ﴿٢﴾
cards.x: He who created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deeds. He is the Mighty, the Forgiving.

The Qur'an calls us again and again to study creation, and true knowledge never contradicts revelation. Where a theory clashes with what the Qur'an states clearly, such as Adam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ being created directly by Allah as the first human, the believer holds to revelation, because theories change and revelation does not.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

cards.x: The hadith reached us through chains of named narrators, each one examined for honesty and precision. Scholars built a whole science to sort the sound from the weak, and no other record of history has been checked like it.
cards.src: Nuzhat al-Nazar, the kinds of hadith

cards.x: Islam gave women the right to own and earn, to inherit, and to consent to marriage. Paradise is at the feet of mothers, and Allah says: 'I will not let the deed of any of you be lost, male or female.'
Do not hide it and do not panic. Write it down, ask a qualified teacher, keep praying and making du'a. Al-Ghazali was cured not by arguing alone but by a light Allah placed in his heart.

checks.q: Why does Allah allow hardship in this world?
checks.a: It is a test, and every wrong is settled on the Day of Judgement
w: Allah does not know about it
checks.why: 'He created death and life to test which of you is best in deeds.'

checks.q: A theory contradicts something the Qur'an states clearly. The believer…
checks.a: Holds to revelation, since theories change
w: Changes the meaning of the Qur'an
checks.why: True knowledge and revelation do not contradict.
checks.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

checks.a: Through chains of named narrators examined for honesty and precision
checks.why: The science of hadith sorts the sound from the weak.
checks.src: Nuzhat al-Nazar, the kinds of hadith

checks.q: You meet a doubt you cannot answer. What is best?
checks.a: Ask a qualified teacher and keep praying
w: Stop practising until it is solved
checks.why: 'Ask the people of knowledge if you do not know.' (al-Nahl 43)

title: Seerah of the Prophet ﷺ
sub: His life ﷺ from birth to his passing
book: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul by Ibn Kathir

lessons.title: His lineage and birth ﷺ
lessons.about: The Prophet's family and early years.

cards.x: Muhammad ﷺ, son of 'Abdullah, son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, son of Hashim, of Quraysh, from the descendants of Isma'il عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his lineage

cards.x: He ﷺ was born on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal, in the Year of the Elephant, according to the sound view.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth and nursing

cards.x: His father died before he was born. His mother Aminah died when he was six, his grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib when he was eight; then his uncle Abu Talib took care of him.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth and nursing

checks.q: On which day was the Prophet ﷺ born?
checks.why: Ibn Kathir: he was born on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal.

checks.q: In which year was he born ﷺ?
checks.why: The sound view is that he was born in the Year of the Elephant.

checks.q: Who raised him after his grandfather died?
checks.why: After 'Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib took care of him.

lessons.title: Childhood and youth ﷺ
lessons.about: With Halimah, Abu Talib, and his marriage to Khadijah.

cards.x: He ﷺ was nursed by Halimah al-Sa'diyyah among Banu Sa'd and stayed with her about four years. There his chest was opened.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

cards.x: His mother took him to visit relatives in Madinah and died at al-Abwa' on the way back, when he was six. Years later, passing al-Abwa' in the year of the Opening, he visited her grave and wept.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

cards.x: At twelve his uncle Abu Talib took him on a trade journey to Syria. Later he travelled there again trading for Khadijah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

cards.x: Khadijah saw his honesty and character and wished to marry him. He married her when he was twenty-five.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

checks.q: Who nursed the Prophet ﷺ?
checks.why: He was nursed among Banu Sa'd by Halimah.

checks.q: Where did his mother pass away?
checks.why: She died at al-Abwa' returning from Madinah.

checks.q: How old was he ﷺ when he married Khadijah?
checks.why: Ibn Kathir: he married her at twenty-five.

lessons.title: The first revelation
lessons.about: The cave of Hira and the first words of the Qur'an.

cards.x: He ﷺ was forty when revelation began. The first to believe was Khadijah; among free men Abu Bakr; among children 'Ali; and among freed slaves Zayd ibn Harithah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ.

cards.ar: اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ ﴿١﴾ خَلَقَ الْإِنسَٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ ﴿٢﴾ اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ ﴿٣﴾ الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ ﴿٤﴾ عَلَّمَ الْإِنسَٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ ﴿٥﴾
cards.x: Read in the name of your Lord who created: created man from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know.
Before prophethood, he ﷺ loved seclusion and would worship in the cave of Hira for nights at a time.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (3)

cards.x: The angel came and said 'Read!' He ﷺ said, 'I am not one who reads.' Then the angel recited: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created…' (al-'Alaq 1–5)
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (3)

cards.x: He returned trembling. Khadijah comforted him: 'Allah will never disgrace you. You keep ties of kinship, carry the burdens of the weak and help the needy.'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (3)

checks.q: Where did the first revelation come?
checks.why: He ﷺ was worshipping in the cave of Hira when the angel came.

checks.a: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created'
w: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful'
'O you wrapped in garments, arise and warn'

checks.q: Who comforted him ﷺ when he came home?
checks.why: Khadijah reassured him that Allah would never disgrace him.

checks.q: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when revelation began?
checks.why: He ﷺ received revelation at forty and lived twenty-three years after it.

lessons.title: Hardship in Makkah
lessons.about: Persecution, Abyssinia and the Year of Sorrow.

cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the trial of the tortured

cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the migration to Abyssinia

cards.x: Quraysh boycotted Banu Hashim. Later the Prophet ﷺ went to Ta'if to call its people, and they drove him out. He returned to Makkah under protection.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the boycott; going out to Ta'if

checks.q: To which land did the first Muslims migrate?

lessons.title: The Year of Sorrow and Ta'if
lessons.about: Losing Khadijah and Abu Talib, and the journey to Ta'if.

cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the journey to Ta'if

checks.a: He hoped their descendants would worship Allah

lessons.title: The pledges of 'Aqabah
lessons.about: How Madinah opened its doors to Islam.

cards.x: At Hajj, twelve men from Yathrib (Madinah) met him ﷺ at 'Aqabah and pledged to worship Allah alone, not steal, not commit zina and not kill their children. He sent Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ with them to teach.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the first 'Aqabah

cards.x: The next year, seventy-three men and two women pledged to protect him ﷺ as they protected their own families. This opened the way to the Hijrah.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the second 'Aqabah

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ send to Madinah to teach after the first pledge?
checks.why: He was the first teacher sent out in Islam.

checks.a: To protect him ﷺ as they protected their own families
w: To pay him a yearly tax

lessons.title: The Night Journey and the Hijrah
lessons.about: From al-Isra' to the arrival in Madinah.

cards.x: Allah took His Messenger ﷺ by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, and up through the heavens. The five daily prayers were made fard on that night.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the Isra' and Mi'raj

cards.ar: سُبْحَٰنَ الَّذِيٓ أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلٗا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَا الَّذِي بَٰرَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ ﴿١﴾
cards.x: Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from the Sacred Masjid to the Furthest Masjid, whose surroundings We have blessed.

cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the first and second pledges of 'Aqabah

cards.x: He ﷺ migrated with Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, hiding in the cave of Thawr, then reached Quba' and Madinah, built the masjid and joined the Muhajirun and Ansar in brotherhood.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the Hijrah; brotherhood

checks.q: What was made fard on the night of the Mi'raj?

checks.q: In which cave did they hide?
checks.why: They hid in the cave of Thawr.

lessons.title: Building Madinah
lessons.about: The masjid, the brotherhood, and a new community.

cards.x: On arriving in Madinah he ﷺ built his masjid, working with his own hands, carrying bricks with the Companions. It was the centre of worship, learning and community.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, building the masjid

checks.q: What was the first thing the Prophet ﷺ built in Madinah?
checks.why: He ﷺ carried bricks with the Companions himself.

lessons.title: Badr, Uhud and the Trench

lessons.title: Hudaybiyah and Khaybar
