checks.q: In which year was the Farewell Hajj?
checks.why: The Farewell Hajj was in the tenth year; he passed away in the eleventh.

lessons.title: The Farewell Hajj
lessons.about: His only Hajj ﷺ, and his last sermon.

cards.x: In 10 AH the Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj with over a hundred thousand Companions. It was his only Hajj, and he taught them its rites, saying: take your rites from me.

cards.ar: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ الْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَالنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بِالْأَزْلَٰمِ ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَٰمَ دِينٗا فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٖ لِّإِثْمٖ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion.
He ﷺ said your blood, wealth and honour are sacred to one another, ended the feuds and riba of the Days of Ignorance, urged kindness to women, and left them the Book of Allah.
At 'Arafah the verse came down: 'Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion.'

checks.q: How many times did the Prophet ﷺ perform Hajj after the Hijrah?
checks.why: It is called the Farewell Hajj.

checks.q: What did he ﷺ declare sacred in the Farewell Sermon?
checks.why: Sacred as that day, that month and that land.

checks.q: Which verse came down at 'Arafah during the Farewell Hajj?
checks.a: 'Today I have perfected your religion for you'
w: 'Read in the name of your Lord'
checks.why: Al-Ma'idah 3.

lessons.title: His passing ﷺ
lessons.about: The last days, and how the Companions held firm.

cards.x: In Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH he ﷺ fell ill. He asked to be nursed in the room of 'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا and told Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ to lead the people in prayer.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his illness

cards.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٞ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ وَمَن يَنقَلِبْ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ اللَّهَ شَيْـٔٗا وَسَيَجْزِي اللَّهُ الشَّـٰكِرِينَ ﴿١٤٤﴾
cards.x: Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?
His last advice included the prayer and kindness to those under your care. He ﷺ passed away on a Monday, aged sixty-three, saying: 'With the highest companion.'
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

cards.x: When some could not believe it, Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ said: whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and never dies. Then he recited Al 'Imran 144.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

checks.q: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when he passed away?
checks.why: He ﷺ received revelation at forty and lived twenty-three years after.

checks.q: Whom did he ﷺ tell to lead the prayer during his final illness?
checks.why: The Companions saw this as a sign of Abu Bakr's precedence.

checks.q: What did Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ remind the people when the Prophet ﷺ passed away?
checks.a: Allah is Ever-Living and never dies
checks.why: Whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and never dies.

lessons.title: His family ﷺ
lessons.about: His children and his wives, the Mothers of the Believers.

cards.x: All his children were from Khadijah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا except Ibrahim, from Mariyah. They were al-Qasim (his kunyah Abu al-Qasim is from him), Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah, 'Abdullah and Ibrahim.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his children

cards.x: All of his children died before him except Fatimah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, who passed away a few months after him.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his children

cards.x: His first wife was Khadijah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, the first to believe in him. He married no one else in her lifetime.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

cards.x: Of his wives, no woman of this Ummah is known to have reached her level of knowledge.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

checks.q: Which of his children outlived him ﷺ?
checks.why: All died before him except Fatimah, who died a few months after.

checks.q: Who was his first wife ﷺ?
checks.why: Khadijah was first, and he married no one else in her lifetime.

checks.q: Why was he called Abu al-Qasim?
checks.why: Al-Qasim was his eldest, and the kunyah is from him.

lessons.title: His character ﷺ
lessons.about: How he looked and how he treated people.

cards.x: Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ described him ﷺ: neither very tall nor short, neither very white nor dark, his hair neither tightly curled nor straight.

cards.ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٖ ﴿٤﴾
cards.x: And truly you are of a tremendous character.

cards.ar: لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٞ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُواْ اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْأٓخِرَ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرٗا ﴿٢١﴾
cards.x: In the Messenger of Allah you have a beautiful example.
Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ served him for ten years, and he ﷺ never once said 'uff' to him, nor asked 'why did you do that?'
'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا was asked about his character. She said: 'His character was the Qur'an.'

checks.q: How long did Anas serve the Prophet ﷺ?
checks.why: Anas served him for ten years and never heard 'uff' from him.

checks.q: How did 'A'ishah describe his character?
checks.why: Her answer: his character was the Qur'an.

checks.q: Which describes his height ﷺ?
w: Tall, like the tallest of them
checks.why: Anas described him as neither very tall nor short.

title: Qur'an: Revelation and Preservation
sub: How the Qur'an came down, was gathered and is preserved

lessons.title: The virtue of the Qur'an
lessons.about: Why learning and reciting it matters, from al-Tibyan.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you is the one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it.'
cards.src: al-Tibyan, chapter one; Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari

cards.x: 'The one skilled in the Qur'an is with the noble, righteous scribes (angels), and the one who stumbles over it and finds it hard has two rewards.'
cards.src: al-Tibyan, chapter one; Hadith, al-Bukhari and Muslim

cards.x: 'Whoever reads a letter of the Book of Allah has a good deed, and a good deed is multiplied ten times. I do not say Alif Lam Mim is a letter: Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter.'

checks.q: Who is 'the best of you', in the hadith?
checks.a: The one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it
w: The one who memorises it but does not teach
The one who fasts and prays the most
The one who gives the most in charity
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari and quoted by al-Nawawi in al-Tibyan.

checks.q: The one who stumbles while reciting…
checks.why: The hadith gives him two rewards for his effort.

checks.q: How many good deeds for one letter?
checks.a: One good deed, multiplied ten times
w: Ten good deeds for each word
One good deed for each verse
checks.why: Each letter is a good deed, multiplied by ten.

lessons.title: How revelation came
lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said about receiving the wahy.

cards.x: Asked how revelation came, he ﷺ said: sometimes it comes like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me; then it leaves me and I have taken in what was said.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (2)

cards.x: 'And sometimes the angel comes to me in the form of a man, speaks to me, and I take in what he says.'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (2)

cards.x: 'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا said she saw revelation come to him on a very cold day, and when it left him his forehead was dripping with sweat.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (2)

checks.q: Which way of revelation did he ﷺ say was hardest?
checks.a: Like the ringing of a bell
checks.why: He said the bell-like way was the hardest on him.

checks.q: In what form did the angel sometimes come?
checks.a: In the form of a man
w: As a voice from a tree
checks.why: 'Sometimes the angel comes to me in the form of a man.'

checks.q: What did 'A'ishah notice on a very cold day?
w: He was shivering from the cold
checks.why: Even on a cold day his forehead dripped with sweat from the weight of revelation.

lessons.title: Revealed bit by bit
lessons.about: Twenty-three years, and Jibril's yearly review.

cards.x: Allah sent the Qur'an down in parts over the years of prophethood: 'A Qur'an We have divided, so that you may recite it to people slowly.' (al-Isra' 106)

cards.ar: وَقُرْءَانٗا فَرَقْنَٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُ عَلَى النَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٖ وَنَزَّلْنَٰهُ تَنزِيلٗا ﴿١٠٦﴾
cards.x: A Qur'an which We have divided into parts, so that you may recite it to people slowly, and We sent it down in stages.
Jibril عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ met the Prophet ﷺ every night of Ramadan and studied the Qur'an with him.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (6)

cards.x: Jibril reviewed the Qur'an with him ﷺ once every year, and twice in the year he passed away.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

checks.q: How was the Qur'an sent down?
w: All of it to him ﷺ in a single day
checks.why: 'A Qur'an We have divided, so that you may recite it slowly.' (al-Isra' 106)

checks.q: When did Jibril study the Qur'an with him ﷺ?
checks.why: Ibn 'Abbas: Jibril met him every night of Ramadan and studied the Qur'an with him.

checks.q: How many times was it reviewed in his final year?
checks.why: Once every year, and twice in the year he passed away.

lessons.title: Gathered into one book
lessons.about: Abu Bakr's collection and 'Uthman's copies.

cards.x: After many reciters were martyred at Yamamah, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ urged Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ to collect the Qur'an. Abu Bakr gave the task to Zayd ibn Thabit رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, a scribe of revelation.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: Zayd gathered it from palm stalks, flat stones and the memories of men. The sheets stayed with Abu Bakr, then 'Umar, then Hafsah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: When Hudhayfah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ saw people differing in recitation, 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ had copies made from Hafsah's sheets and sent one to each region.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

checks.q: Who first ordered the Qur'an to be collected into one book?
checks.why: Abu Bakr ordered it, on 'Umar's advice, after Yamamah.

checks.q: Who did the collecting?
checks.a: Zayd ibn Thabit رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
checks.why: Zayd ibn Thabit, a scribe of revelation, was given the task.

checks.q: Why did 'Uthman send copies to the regions?
checks.why: Hudhayfah warned him of differences, so he sent unified copies from Hafsah's sheets.

lessons.title: Preserved by Allah
lessons.about: Seven modes, memorisers, and Allah's promise.

cards.x: 'Indeed it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will preserve it.' (al-Hijr 9)

cards.ar: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَٰفِظُونَ ﴿٩﴾
cards.x: Truly, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and truly We will preserve it.

'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ heard Hisham ibn Hakim رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ recite differently and brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, who approved both and said the Qur'an was revealed in seven modes (ahruf).
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: The Qur'an is preserved in hearts as well as written in copies, as Imam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ said. Every generation has had countless people who memorised it.

checks.q: Who preserves the Qur'an, according to al-Hijr 9?
checks.why: 'It is We who sent down the Reminder, and We will preserve it.'

checks.q: In how many modes (ahruf) was the Qur'an revealed?
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said it was revealed in seven ahruf.

checks.q: When 'Umar and Hisham recited differently, the Prophet ﷺ…
checks.why: He approved both and explained the seven modes.

lessons.title: Honouring the Qur'an
lessons.about: Al-Nawawi's manners with the Book of Allah.

cards.x: Recite in a state of purity, with a clean mouth, using the siwak, facing the qiblah and sitting with humility.
cards.src: al-Tibyan fi Adab Hamalat al-Qur'an, manners of the Qur'an

cards.ar: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا ﴿٤﴾
cards.x: And recite the Qur'an in measured recitation (tartil).

cards.ar: لَّا يَمَسُّهُٓ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ ﴿٧٩﴾
cards.x: None touch it except the purified.
Recite with tartil, reflecting on the meaning. Reflection is the whole purpose of recitation.
cards.src: al-Tibyan fi Adab Hamalat al-Qur'an, manners of the Qur'an

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, a person without wudu may not touch the Qur'an except with a separate cover. Someone in janabah may not recite it either.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what is forbidden without purity

checks.q: According to al-Nawawi, what is the purpose of recitation?
checks.why: Al-Nawawi says reflection is the point of reciting.

checks.q: Without wudu, may you touch the Qur'an in the Hanafi school?
checks.a: No, only with a separate cover
checks.why: Nur al-Idah lists touching the Qur'an among what is forbidden without purity.

checks.q: Which is a manner of recitation al-Nawawi mentions?
checks.why: A clean mouth and siwak are among the manners he gives.

title: Tazkiyah
sub: Sincerity, repentance and the illnesses of the heart

lessons.title: Sincerity
lessons.about: Why you seek knowledge, and the weight of intention.

cards.x: Imam al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ begins by asking why you seek knowledge. If it is to compete, show off and win people's attention, you are tearing down your religion. If it is for guidance, the angels spread their wings for you as you walk.

cards.ar: وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُواْ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُواْ الصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُواْ الزَّكَوٰةَ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ ﴿٥﴾
cards.x: They were only commanded to worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His.
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Actions are only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended.'

checks.q: According to al-Ghazali, seeking knowledge to show off…
w: Is fine if the knowledge is true
checks.why: Al-Ghazali says seeking knowledge to compete and show off tears down your religion.

checks.q: According to the hadith, actions are judged by…
checks.why: 'Actions are only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended.'

checks.q: Which deeds are accepted by Allah?
checks.why: 'Actions are only by intentions.' Sincerity is the soul of every deed.

checks.q: You notice you want praise for a good deed. What should you do?
checks.a: Correct your intention and keep doing it for Allah
checks.why: Don't leave good deeds for fear of riya'; purify the intention.

lessons.title: Repentance
lessons.about: What tawbah is and its three conditions.

cards.x: Repentance (tawbah) means turning back from what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةٗ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّـٰتٖ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَٰرُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَآ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٖ قَدِيرٞ ﴿٨﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance.

cards.ar: وَقُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحْفَظْنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوْ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ التَّـٰبِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُوْلِي الْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ أَوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَٰتِ النِّسَآءِ وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: And turn to Allah all together, O believers, so that you may succeed.
Regret for what you did, stopping the sin straight away, and resolving never to return to it.
If the sin wronged another person, there is a fourth condition: freeing yourself of their right, by returning what you took or asking their forgiveness.

checks.q: Which is a condition of repentance?
checks.why: Regret is one of the three conditions, with stopping the sin and resolving never to return.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, chapter on repentance · Riyad al-Salihin, chapter on repentance

checks.q: How many conditions does al-Qushayri give for repentance?
checks.why: Al-Qushayri gives three: regret, stopping straight away, and resolving never to go back.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, chapter on repentance · Riyad al-Salihin, chapter on repentance

checks.q: Repentance means turning…
checks.a: From what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises
w: From one school of law to another
From people to a life alone
checks.why: Tawbah is turning back from what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises.

lessons.title: Walking the path
lessons.about: Turning what you have learnt into a daily practice, with a guide.

title: The Companions and Ahl al-Bayt
sub: The four caliphs, the ten, the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet's family ﷺ

lessons.title: Who the Companions are
lessons.about: Their rank, and why we love them.

cards.x: A Companion (sahabi) is someone who met the Prophet ﷺ as a believer and died as a Muslim. They carried the Qur'an and the Sunnah to us.

cards.ar: وَالسَّـٰبِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ الْمُهَٰجِرِينَ وَالْأَنصَارِ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُم بِإِحْسَٰنٖ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُواْ عَنْهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّـٰتٖ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدٗا ذَٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ ﴿١٠٠﴾
cards.x: And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them in excellence: Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him.

cards.ar: مُّحَمَّدٞ رَّسُولُ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ تَرَىٰهُمْ رُكَّعٗا سُجَّدٗا يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلٗا مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنٗا سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَىٰةِ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْـَٔهُ فَـَٔازَرَهُ فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فَاسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّـٰلِحَٰتِ مِنْهُم مَّغْفِرَةٗ وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمَا ﴿٢٩﴾
cards.x: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers, merciful to one another.

The Prophet ﷺ said: the best of people are my generation, then those after them, then those after them. Allah said He is pleased with the foremost Muhajirun and Ansar, and those who follow them in excellence.

We love them all, go to excess about none of them, disown none, speak of them only with good, and keep silent about the disputes between them. Loving them is religion and faith; hating them is disbelief, hypocrisy and transgression.

checks.why: They were people of excellence; Allah will judge between them.

checks.q: Loving the Companions is, according to al-Tahawi…
checks.why: And hating them is disbelief, hypocrisy and transgression.

lessons.title: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
lessons.about: The first caliph, and the best of the Ummah after its Prophet ﷺ.

cards.x: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Quhafah, the first free man to believe. He was called al-Siddiq (the truthful) for affirming the Night Journey at once: 'If he said it, then it is true.'

cards.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا فَأَنزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٖ لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ السُّفْلَىٰ وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ ﴿٤٠﴾
cards.x: …the second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: 'Do not grieve, Allah is with us.'
He accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah and hid with him in the Cave of Thawr. Allah mentions him: 'the second of two, when they were in the cave.'
He was caliph for about two years. He stood firm against those who refused zakat and against the false prophets, and began the gathering of the Qur'an into one volume.

checks.q: Why was Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ called al-Siddiq?
checks.a: For affirming the Prophet ﷺ at once, as with the Night Journey
checks.why: 'If he said it, then it is true.'

lessons.title: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
lessons.about: Al-Faruq, the second caliph.

cards.x: His acceptance of Islam was a great strength for the Muslims; after it they prayed openly at the Ka'bah. He was named al-Faruq, the one who separates truth from falsehood.
Caliph for ten years, he was known for justice and fearing Allah. Under him Syria, Iraq, Persia and Egypt opened, and Jerusalem was received peacefully.
He began the Hijri calendar, gathered the people for tarawih behind one imam, and set up the public treasury and offices. He was martyred while leading the Fajr prayer.

checks.q: What title was 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ given?
checks.why: The one who separates truth from falsehood.

checks.q: Which calendar did 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ begin?
checks.why: Counting from the Hijrah of the Prophet ﷺ.

checks.q: How was 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ martyred?
checks.a: Stabbed while leading the Fajr prayer
checks.why: He was stabbed by Abu Lu'lu'ah in the masjid.

checks.q: Which city was received peacefully in 'Umar's caliphate?
checks.why: 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ travelled to receive it himself.

lessons.title: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
lessons.about: Dhu al-Nurayn, the third caliph.

cards.x: He married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ, Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, and was called Dhu al-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights. He was known for his modesty; even the angels were shy of him.
He bought the well of Rumah for the Muslims and equipped the army of Tabuk from his own wealth.
As caliph for twelve years, he had the Qur'an copied in one standard text from Abu Bakr's volume and sent to the cities. He was martyred in his house while reading the Qur'an.

checks.q: Why was 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ called Dhu al-Nurayn?
checks.a: He married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ
checks.why: Ruqayyah, then after her death Umm Kulthum رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا.

checks.q: What did 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ do with the Qur'an?

w: First gathered it into one volume
checks.why: Abu Bakr gathered it; 'Uthman made the standard copies.

checks.q: Which quality was 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ especially known for?
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said: shall I not be shy of a man of whom the angels are shy?

lessons.title: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

cards.x: He was raised in the Prophet's home and was the first child to accept Islam. He slept in the Prophet's bed on the night of the Hijrah, and married Fatimah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا.

lessons.title: The Mothers of the Believers
lessons.about: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

cards.x: Allah called the Prophet's wives the Mothers of the Believers. We honour them as our mothers.

cards.ar: النَّبِيُّ أَوْلَىٰ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُهُٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمْ وَأُوْلُواْ الْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٖ فِي كِتَٰبِ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُهَٰجِرِينَ إِلَّآ أَن تَفْعَلُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِكُم مَّعْرُوفٗا كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي الْكِتَٰبِ مَسْطُورٗا ﴿٦﴾
cards.x: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers.

cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

checks.q: What did Allah call the wives of the Prophet ﷺ?
checks.why: 'And his wives are their mothers.' (al-Ahzab 6)

checks.q: Who was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ and the first to believe?
checks.why: She supported him with her wealth and her heart.

checks.q: Which Mother of the Believers was among the most learned of the Companions?
checks.why: Senior Companions came to her with their questions.

checks.q: Hafsah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا was the daughter of…
checks.why: 'A'ishah was the daughter of Abu Bakr.

lessons.title: The Ahl al-Bayt
lessons.about: The family of the Prophet ﷺ, and loving them.

cards.x: The Ahl al-Bayt are the family of the Prophet ﷺ: his wives, Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and their descendants, and the believers of Banu Hashim. Zakat may not be given to them, out of honour.

cards.ar: وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ الْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ الْأُولَىٰ وَأَقِمْنَ الصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ الزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعْنَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُٓ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرٗا ﴿٣٣﴾
cards.x: Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O people of the House, and to purify you completely.
His youngest daughter. He ﷺ said: Fatimah is a part of me; whoever angers her angers me. She is the leader of the women of Paradise.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of the Companions

cards.x: He ﷺ called them his two sweet basils of this world, and said they are the leaders of the youth of Paradise. Al-Husayn رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was martyred at Karbala in 61 AH, a great tragedy for the Ummah.
He ﷺ said: I leave among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah, and the people of my house. I remind you of Allah regarding the people of my house. Loving them is part of loving him.
cards.src: Sahih Muslim, Virtues of the Companions

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ call the leaders of the youth of Paradise?
checks.a: Al-Hasan and al-Husayn رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا
w: Abu Bakr and 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا
Zayd and Usamah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

checks.q: Where was al-Husayn رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ martyred?
checks.why: In 61 AH, on the day of 'Ashura'.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say he left among us, in Sahih Muslim?
checks.a: The Book of Allah and the people of his house
checks.why: 'I remind you of Allah regarding the people of my house,' three times.

checks.q: Why may zakat not be given to Banu Hashim?
checks.a: Out of honour for the Prophet's family ﷺ
checks.why: Help them with gifts and charity that is not zakat.

lessons.title: Loving both, the way of Ahl al-Sunnah
lessons.about: Holding the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt together in the heart.

cards.x: Ahl al-Sunnah love the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt together, with no contradiction. 'Ali named his sons Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman, and 'Umar married Umm Kulthum, daughter of 'Ali and Fatimah.
We believe the caliphate after the Prophet ﷺ was for Abu Bakr, then 'Umar, then 'Uthman, then 'Ali, the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and their excellence is in that order.
We do not curse any Companion, as some do, and we do not belittle the Ahl al-Bayt, as others do. Whoever speaks well of the Companions, the Prophet's wives and his descendants is free of hypocrisy.

checks.q: Who are the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, in order?
checks.why: Their excellence follows the order of their caliphate.

checks.q: Which shows the love between 'Ali and the other caliphs?
checks.a: 'Ali named his sons Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman
checks.why: Names a father gives his sons show his love.

checks.q: What is the way of Ahl al-Sunnah with the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt?
checks.a: To love both, and curse none
w: To love the Ahl al-Bayt only
To stay neutral and love neither
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: whoever speaks well of them is free of hypocrisy.

title: Daily life: adab and adhkar
sub: The sunnah way to wake, eat, dress, greet, sleep, and guard the limbs
book: Bidayat al-Hidayah, al-Adhkar and Riyad al-Salihin

lessons.title: Waking up and the morning
lessons.about: Starting the day the sunnah way.

cards.x: Say: 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhi al-nushur' (praise be to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the return). Use the siwak.
Al-Ghazali advises waking before dawn, making wudu, praying the two sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr at home, then going to pray Fajr in congregation.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of waking

cards.x: Sitting in remembrance of Allah after Fajr until the sun has risen, then praying two rak'ahs, carries the reward of a complete Hajj and 'umrah, as in the hadith.

checks.q: What do you say on waking up?
checks.a: 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana…'
checks.why: Praise to Allah who gave us life after death (sleep). The second option is said before sleeping.

checks.q: What reward is in the hadith for staying in dhikr after Fajr until sunrise, then praying two rak'ahs?
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

checks.q: Where does al-Ghazali advise praying the sunnah of Fajr?
checks.a: At home, before going to the masjid
checks.why: The sunnah prayers are best at home.

lessons.title: Morning and evening adhkar
lessons.about: The daily protection every Muslim should keep.

cards.x: Recite Surat al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas three times in the morning and three in the evening; the Prophet ﷺ said they will suffice you against everything.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Manners

cards.x: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi in the morning is protected until evening, and in the evening until morning.
'Allahumma anta rabbi, la ilaha illa ant, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduk…' Whoever says it with certainty in the morning and dies that day is of the people of Paradise; the same for the evening.
'Subhan Allahi wa bi-hamdih' a hundred times a day wipes away sins even if they are like the foam of the sea.

checks.q: How many times are the three Quls recited morning and evening?
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said they suffice against everything.

checks.q: What is 'Sayyid al-Istighfar'?
checks.a: The master of seeking forgiveness: 'Allahumma anta rabbi…'
checks.why: Said with certainty morning or evening, it is a means to Paradise.

checks.q: Saying 'Subhan Allahi wa bi-hamdih' a hundred times a day…
checks.a: Wipes away sins, even like the foam of the sea
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari.

checks.q: Which verse protects you from morning until evening when recited?
w: The last verse of al-Baqarah only
checks.why: Al-Baqarah 255.

lessons.title: After the prayer
lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said after every fard prayer.

cards.x: After the salam, say 'Astaghfirullah' three times, then 'Allahumma anta al-salam wa minka al-salam, tabarakta ya dha al-jalali wa al-ikram.'

Say 'Subhan Allah' 33 times, 'Al-hamdu lillah' 33 times and 'Allahu akbar' 34 times (or 33 and then 'La ilaha illa Allahu wahdahu la sharika lah…'). Sins are forgiven even if like the foam of the sea.
Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every fard prayer, nothing stands between him and Paradise except death.
cards.src: Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, After the prayer

checks.q: What is said three times right after the salam?
checks.why: Then 'Allahumma anta al-salam…'.

checks.q: How many times is 'Allahu akbar' said in the tasbih after prayer?
checks.why: 33 Subhan Allah, 33 Al-hamdu lillah, 34 Allahu akbar.

checks.q: What reward is mentioned for Ayat al-Kursi after every fard prayer?
checks.a: Only death stands between him and Paradise
checks.why: Narrated by al-Nasa'i.

lessons.title: Greeting with salam
lessons.about: Spreading salam, and how to reply.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you what will make you love one another? Spread salam among you.

cards.ar: وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٖ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَآ أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا ﴿٨٦﴾
cards.x: When you are greeted with a greeting, reply with a better one, or return it.
Beginning the salam is a sunnah; replying is wajib. Reply with the same or better: to 'al-salamu 'alaykum' reply 'wa 'alaykum al-salam wa rahmatullah'.
cards.src: Riyad al-Salihin, the chapter on salam

cards.x: The rider greets the one walking, the walker the one sitting, the smaller group the larger, and the young the old.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Seeking Permission

checks.q: What is the ruling of replying to a salam?
checks.why: Beginning it is sunnah; replying is wajib.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say makes people love one another?
checks.why: Narrated by Muslim.

checks.q: Who should greet first, the one walking or the one sitting?
checks.why: And the rider greets the walker, the few greet the many.

checks.q: Someone says 'al-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah'. What is the better reply?
checks.why: Reply with the same or better.

lessons.title: Eating and drinking
lessons.about: The sunnahs of the table.

cards.x: Wash the hands, say 'Bismillah', and eat with the right hand from what is in front of you. If you forget bismillah, say 'Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah.'

cards.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٖ وَكُلُواْ وَاشْرَبُواْ وَلَا تُسْرِفُوٓاْ إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: Eat and drink, but do not waste. Truly He does not love the wasteful.
Do not fill the stomach: a third for food, a third for drink and a third for breath. Never criticise food: eat it if you like it, leave it if you don't.
Drink sitting, in three breaths, with the right hand, and not from the mouth of a container. Gold and silver vessels are haram.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of eating

cards.x: Lick the fingers, and say 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi at'amani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah.'
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Clothing

checks.q: You forgot to say bismillah at the start of the meal. What do you say?
checks.why: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.

checks.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the right amount to eat?
checks.a: A third food, a third drink, a third breath
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

checks.q: Which hand do you eat and drink with?
checks.why: Shaytan eats and drinks with his left.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ do with food he did not like?
checks.a: He left it without criticising it
w: He criticised it to teach others
checks.why: He never found fault with food.

lessons.title: Dressing and the sunnahs of the body
lessons.about: Clothing, and the fitrah.

cards.x: Begin with the right when dressing and the left when undressing. Say 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi kasani hadha wa razaqanihi…' when putting on clothes.
Gold and silk are haram for men. A man's garment should not drag below the ankles out of pride.
The acts of the fitrah: circumcision, removing pubic hair, plucking the armpits, trimming the moustache and clipping the nails. Do not leave them more than forty days.

checks.q: Which foot or sleeve do you begin with when dressing?
checks.why: Right when dressing, left when undressing.

checks.q: What is the longest these acts of the fitrah should be left?
checks.why: Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrated the limit of forty days.

checks.q: Which of these is haram for men to wear?
checks.why: A silver ring of modest weight is allowed for men.

lessons.title: The home and the masjid
lessons.about: Entering, leaving, and the adab of the masjid.

cards.x: Say: 'Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'ala Allah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.' It is said to him: you are guided, protected and sufficed.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Manners

cards.x: Enter with the right foot saying 'Allahumma iftah li abwaba rahmatik', and leave with the left saying 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik.' Pray two rak'ahs greeting the masjid before sitting.
Do not come after eating raw onion or garlic, do not raise your voice, do not pass in front of someone praying, and do not trade or look for lost things in it.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of the masjid

checks.q: With which foot do you enter the masjid?
checks.why: Right to enter the masjid; left to enter the toilet.

checks.q: What do you say when entering the masjid?
checks.why: Open for me the doors of Your mercy. The second is said when leaving.

checks.q: What should you avoid before going to the masjid?
checks.why: Their smell harms the people and the angels.

checks.q: What is the prayer on entering the masjid before sitting?
checks.why: Tahiyyat al-masjid, at a time when prayer is not disliked.

lessons.title: Sneezing, the sick and the funeral
lessons.about: Small acts with great reward.

cards.x: Whoever sneezes says 'Al-hamdu lillah'; the one who hears replies 'Yarhamuk Allah'; the sneezer answers 'Yahdikumu Allahu wa yuslihu balakum.' When yawning, cover the mouth and hold it back as much as you can.
Visiting the sick is among the rights of a Muslim. Whoever visits a sick person is among the fruits of Paradise until he returns. Pray for him: 'La ba's, tahurun in sha' Allah.'

Six rights of a Muslim over another: return his salam, answer his invitation, give him sincere advice, reply when he sneezes and praises Allah, visit him when ill, and follow his funeral when he dies.

checks.q: Someone sneezes and says 'Al-hamdu lillah'. What do you reply?
checks.why: May Allah have mercy on you.

checks.q: Which is one of the six rights of a Muslim over another?
checks.a: To visit him when he is ill
w: To lend him money whenever asked
checks.why: Narrated by Muslim.

checks.q: What should you do when yawning?
checks.a: Cover the mouth and hold it back
checks.why: Yawning is from Shaytan; hold it back as much as you can.

lessons.title: Before sleeping
lessons.about: Ending the day the sunnah way.

cards.x: Sleep in wudu, dust the bed, lie on the right side with the right hand under the cheek. Close the doors and cover the vessels saying bismillah.
Ayat al-Kursi, the three Quls (blowing into the hands and wiping over the body three times), the last two verses of al-Baqarah, and 'Subhan Allah' 33, 'Al-hamdu lillah' 33, 'Allahu akbar' 34.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: Say 'Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya' (in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live), and take account of your day: thank Allah for the good and repent of the wrong.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of sleeping

checks.q: On which side is it sunnah to sleep?
checks.why: With the right hand under the cheek.

checks.q: What do you say just before sleeping?
checks.why: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

checks.q: Which tasbih did the Prophet ﷺ teach 'Ali and Fatimah for bedtime?
checks.a: 33 Subhan Allah, 33 Al-hamdu lillah, 34 Allahu akbar
checks.why: He said it is better for them than a servant.

checks.q: What does al-Ghazali advise doing before sleep?
checks.why: Thank Allah for the good and repent of the wrong.

lessons.title: Guarding the seven limbs
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's guide to avoiding sins.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali says religion has two parts: doing what is commanded and leaving what is forbidden, and leaving sins is the harder and more important. Guard seven limbs: the eyes, ears, tongue, stomach, private parts, hands and feet.

cards.ar: وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولٗا ﴿٣٦﴾
cards.x: Do not follow what you have no knowledge of. Truly the hearing, the sight and the heart: each of these will be asked about.
Lower the gaze from what is haram, and do not look at a Muslim with contempt. Do not listen to backbiting, obscenity or idle talk about others' faults; the listener shares the sin of the speaker.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the eye and the ear

cards.x: Guard it from eight things: lying, breaking promises, backbiting, arguing, praising yourself, cursing, praying against people, and joking that hurts or mocks.
Eat only halal, and not too much. Do not use the hands to harm, take or write what is haram. Do not walk to a ruler's door to flatter, or anywhere sinful.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the stomach, hands and feet

checks.q: According to al-Ghazali, which part of religion is harder: doing good, or leaving sins?
checks.why: Anyone can do good deeds; only the truthful leave their desires.

checks.q: Listening to backbiting…
checks.a: Shares in the sin of the speaker
w: Is fine if you say nothing
Is good, to know what is happening
checks.why: Stop it, leave, or at least hate it in your heart.

checks.q: Which of these is among the eight sins of the tongue al-Ghazali lists?
checks.why: Along with lying, broken promises, backbiting, arguing, cursing, praying against others and hurtful joking.

checks.q: How many limbs does al-Ghazali tell us to guard?
checks.why: Eyes, ears, tongue, stomach, private parts, hands and feet.

lessons.title: Seeking knowledge and passing it on
lessons.about: You have learnt the basics. Now keep learning, and teach.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: seeking knowledge is an obligation on every Muslim. Al-Ghazali explains that fard al-'ayn grows with your situation: when a prayer time comes you must know how to pray; before you marry, learn the rulings of marriage; before you trade, learn the rulings of trade. Going deeper is a virtue, and some must do it for the whole community.

cards.ar: فَتَعَٰلَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمٗا ﴿١١٤﴾
cards.x: And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

cards.ar: أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ الَّيْلِ سَاجِدٗا وَقَآئِمٗا يَحْذَرُ الْأٓخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُواْ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ الْأَلْبَٰبِ ﴿٩﴾
cards.x: Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?
He ﷺ said: convey from me, even one verse. And: whoever guides to good has the reward of the one who does it. Teach your family first what you have learnt.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

cards.x: Teach only what you know well, say 'I don't know' when you don't, mention your source, be gentle and make it easy.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of the scholar

cards.x: Al-Ghazali warns: knowledge that is not acted on is a proof against you. Act on what you learn, then study further with a teacher, in the Course and in our live classes.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about passing on knowledge?
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari.

checks.q: Someone asks you a question you are unsure about. What should you do?
checks.a: Say 'I don't know', or refer them to a scholar
w: Guess so you don't look ignorant
checks.why: Speaking about the religion without knowledge is a grave sin; 'I don't know' protects you.

checks.q: Who should you teach first?
checks.why: 'Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire.' (al-Tahrim 6)

checks.q: What does al-Ghazali say about knowledge that is not acted on?
checks.a: It is a proof against you
checks.why: Act on what you learn.
